semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ}: like His saying {لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ} [al-Naḥl: 5]. And «حين» is accusative (manṣūb) by «جَمال» itself, or by an omitted [word] on the basis that it is a naʿt (adjective) of it, or it is governed by what governs «فيها» or «لكم».
ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «حينا» with tanwīn, on the basis that the clause after it is a naʿt of it, and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. "a time in which you bring them home, and a time in which you send them out to pasture", like His saying, the Exalted: {واتقوا يَوْماً تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 281].
Bringing home (al-irāḥa) was placed before sending out to pasture (al-sarḥ) because the livestock are more beautiful then, with their bellies full and their udders swollen with milk.
Al-jamāl (beauty) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of jamula (with ḍamma on the mīm), yajmulu, so he is jamīl and she is jamīla. Al-Kisāʾī reported jamlāʾ, like ḥamrāʾ, and recited:
295 - 7- فهِيَ جَمْلاءُ كَبَدْرٍ طالعٍ ... بَذَّتِ الخَلْقَ جميعاً بالجَمالْ
(She is beautiful (jamlāʾ) like a rising full moon; she surpassed all creatures in beauty.)
One says: arāḥa al-māshiya (he brought the livestock home) and harāḥahā, with hāʾ in place of the hamza. And saraḥa al-ibila, yasraḥuhā, sarḥan, i.e. he sent them out; its origin is that he sends them out to graze on the sarḥ, and the sarḥ is a tree that bears fruit, the singular being sarḥa. He said:
295 - 8- أبى اللهُ إلا أنَّ سَرْحَةَ مالكٍ ... على كلِّ افنانِ العِضاهِ تَرُوْقُ
(Allah has willed only that Mālik's sarḥa tree should excel over all the branches of the thorny trees.)
And he said:
295 - 9- بَطَلٌ كأن ثيابَه في سَرْحةٍ ... يُحْذَى نِعالَ السَّبْتِ ليس بتوْءَم
(A hero, as though his garments were on a sarḥa tree [for his tallness]; he is shod with tanned-leather sandals, and he is not a twin.)
Then it was applied to every sending forth, and it was also borrowed for divorce, so they said: sarraḥa fulānun imraʾatahu (so-and-so released his wife), just as divorce (ṭalāq) was also borrowed from releasing (iṭlāq) camels from their tethers. And from al-sarḥ the sense of going on was taken, so it was said: nāqa suruḥ, i.e. a swift she-camel. He said:
296 - 0-. . . سُرُحُ اليَدَيْن. . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… swift of forelegs …)
The objects of «تُرِيْحون» and «تَسْرَحُون» were omitted out of regard for the verse-endings (fawāṣil), since they are known.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَّمْ تَكُونُواْ}: a naʿt (adjective) of «بلد», and «إلا بشِقٍّ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in «بالِغِيْه», i.e. "you would not reach it except while beset with hardship."
The majority read it with kasra on the shīn. Abū Jaʿfar read it with fatḥa, and this was also narrated from Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr. It was said: they are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) with one meaning, i.e. hardship (al-mashaqqa); from the kasra form is his saying:
296 - 1- رأى إبِلاً تَسْعى، ويَحْسِبُها له ... أخي نَصَبٍ مِنْ شِقِّها ودُؤْوْبِ
(He saw camels on the move, and he reckons them his own — one of toil, from their hardship (shiqq) and constant labour.)
i.e. from their hardship. / It was said: the form with fatḥa is the maṣdar and the form with kasra is the noun. It was said: with kasra it means half of a thing. In the exegesis: "except with half of yourselves", just as you say "you will not attain it except with a piece of your liver", figuratively.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والخيل}: The majority read it in the accusative, conjoined to «الأنعامَ». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being omitted, i.e. "created" or "prepared for you to ride"; and this is not a case where the preposition with its noun stands in place of the khabar, because it is a specific being (kawn khāṣṣ).
His saying: «وزينةً»: there are several views on its accusative. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the verb reached the first one by means of the lām in His saying «لتركبوها», and reached this one by itself, because a condition is lacking in the first, namely that the agent is not the same: the Creator is Allah, while the riders are those addressed — unlike the second.
The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the one it describes being either the object of «خَلَقَها» or the object of «لتركبوها»; so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of a ḥāl.
The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb; al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as «وخَلَقها زينة» ("and He created them as adornment"), and Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others estimated it as «وجَعَلها زينةً» ("and He made them an adornment").
The fourth: that it is the maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e. "and they adorn themselves with them with adornment."
Qatāda read, from Ibn ʿAbbās, «لتَرْكَبوها زينةً» without the wāw; the views mentioned above apply to it, with the addition that it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «لتركبوها», i.e. "you ride them adorning yourselves with them."

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌ}: The pronoun refers back to «السبيل» because it is treated as feminine: {قُلْ هذه سبيلي} [Yūsuf: 108]; or because it carries the meaning of «سُبُل» (paths), so it was made feminine according to the meaning of the plural.
Al-qaṣd is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description, so it means qāṣid; one says sabīlun qaṣdun and qāṣidun, i.e. straight, as though it heads for the direction the traveller aims at without deviating from it. It was said: the pronoun refers back to the creatures, and this is supported by the reading of ʿĪsā and what is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: «ومنكم جائِزٌ», and the reading of ʿAlī: «فمنكم جائر» with fāʾ. [Translator's note: the codex reading is printed «جائِزٌ» with zāy, while ʿAlī's is «جائر»; translated as written.]
It was said: the al- in «السبيل» is for something previously known (ʿahd); on this view the pronoun refers back to the "path" implied by the meaning of the verse, as though it were said: "and of the paths", so it referred back to it although it had not been mentioned, because its counterpart indicates it. But if the al- is generic, then it refers back to its wording.
Al-jawr: deviating from straightness. Al-Nābigha said:
296 - 2-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يَجُور بها الملاَّحُ طَوْراً ويَهْتدي
(… the sailor veers off course with it at times, and at times keeps the right way.)
And another said:
296 - 3- ومن الطريقةِ جائرٌ وهُدىً ... قَصْدُ السبيلِ ومنه ذُو دَخْلِ
(Of the way some is deviating and some is guidance; the path is straight, and of it is some that is corrupt.)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«قَصْدُ» is a maṣdar meaning the setting-straight of the path and the levelling of the path; it is not the maṣdar of qaṣadtuhu in the sense of 'I came to him'."

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَآءً لَّكُم مَّنْهُ شَرَابٌ}: «لكم» may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنْزَلَ», and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «ماءً», so it is attached to an omitted [word]. On the first view «شرابٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «منه» is its khabar (predicate) placed before it, and the clause is likewise a naʿt of «ماءً»; on the second view «شرابٌ» is a fāʿil (agent) of the adverbial phrase, and «منه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شراب». The first «مِنْ» is partitive, and so is the second according to some of them, but it is figurative, because since [the tree's] watering is by the water, it was treated as though it were from the water, like his saying:
294 - 6- أسنِمَة الآبالِ في رَبابَهْ ...
(The camels' humps are in a white cloud.)
i.e. in a cloud, by which he means the rain by which the pasture grows that the camels eat, so that their humps grow fat. [Translator's note: the verse number is printed «294 - 6» in the source, out of sequence; reproduced as written.]
Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī said: "It involves the omission of a muḍāf, either from the first, meaning before the pronoun, i.e. 'from its watering and its means are trees', or from the second, meaning before «شجر», i.e. 'the drink of trees' or 'the life of trees'." Abū al-Baqāʾ made the first partitive and the second causal, i.e. "by its cause", and this is indicated by His saying: {يُنبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزرع}. [Translator's note: the source discusses «ومنه شجر», part of the same verse, without quoting it in the heading.]
Al-shajar here is every plant of the earth, even pasture-grass; in the ḥadīth: "Do not eat the shajar, for it is unlawful (suḥt)", meaning pasture-grass; it forbids fencing off freely available things that are badly needed. And he said:
296 - 5- نُطْعِمُها اللحمَ إذا عَزَّ الشجَرْ ...
(We feed them meat when the shajar [pasture] is scarce.)
And that is figurative, because shajar is what has a trunk.
His saying: {فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ}: this is another naʿt of «ماءً». The majority read «تُسِيمون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from asāma, i.e. he sent them out to graze; and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with fatḥa, so it may be transitive, faʿala and afʿala having the same meaning, or it may be intransitive with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "your livestock graze." [Translator's note: the source says "the yāʾ", although the word is written with tāʾ; translated as written.]

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يُنبِتُ}: this clause may be resumptive or subordinate, as in its counterpart. One says "anbata Allāhu al-zarʿa" (Allah made the crops grow), so it is manbūt, though by analogy it should be munbat. It was said: anbata sometimes comes intransitive, like nabata; al-Farrāʾ recited:
296 - 6- رأيتَ ذوي الحاجاتِ حولَ بيوتِهمْ ... قَطِيناً لهم حتى إذا أَنْبَتَ البَقْلُ
(You saw the needy around their houses, staying with them until the herbage sprouted (anbata).)
Al-Aṣmaʿī rejected that, but the verse is proof against him, and interpreting it as "the herbage made itself grow", figuratively, is very far-fetched.
Abū Bakr read «نُنْبِتُ» with the nūn of majesty, / and al-Zuhrī «نُنَبِّتُ» with doubling. The apparent view is that it is the doubling of the transitive verb; it was said rather that it is for repetition. Ubayy read «يَنْبُت» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the bāʾ, with «الزَّرعُ» and what follows it nominative as agents.

semin-durr:12-12.t: The disagreement of the readers about reading «الشمس» and what follows it in the nominative or the accusative, and the justification of that, has already been given in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا ذَرَأَ}: conjoined to «الليل», as al-Zamakhsharī said, meaning the animals and trees He created in it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "In the position of an accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. 'and He created and caused to grow'." It is as though he thought it unlikely that «سَخَّر» governs that, so he estimated a fitting verb. «مختلفاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, and «ألوانُه» is its fāʿil (agent).
He closed the first verse with reflection, because what is in it needs contemplation and consideration; the second with reason, because what precedes turns on it; and the third with remembrance, because it is the result of what preceded. He made «آيات» plural in the second but not in the first and third, because more is connected to it, and for that reason He mentioned reason with it.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِنْهُ لَحْماً}: «منه» may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لتأكلوا», or to an omitted [word] because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the indefinite noun after it. «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent or partitive, and the omission of a muḍāf is necessary, i.e. "from its animals".
«طَرِيّاً» is of the pattern faʿīl from ṭaruwa, yaṭrū, ṭarāwatan, like saruwa, yasrū, sarāwatan. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Rather one says ṭariya, yaṭrā, ṭarāwatan and ṭarāʾan, like shaqiya, yashqā, shaqāwatan and shaqāʾan." Al-ṭarāwa is the opposite of dryness, i.e. fresh and new. One says: al-thiyāb al-muṭarrāt (freshened garments). And al-iṭrāʾ is praise whose mention is renewed. As for ṭaraʾa with hamza, it means "to appear".
His saying: «حِلْيةً»: al-ḥilya is a noun for that with which one adorns oneself, and its origin is to denote a manner, like al-ʿimma and al-khimra. «تَلْبَسُونها» is a naʿt (adjective). «منه» allows what was allowed for the «منه» before it. His saying «تَرَى» is a parenthetical clause between the two causal clauses, namely «لتأكلوا» and «لِتَبْتَغُوا»; it is parenthetical only because it addresses one person between two addresses to a group.
His saying: «فيه» may be attached to «ترى», or to «مواخِرَ» because it means "cleaving", or to an omitted [word] because it is a ḥāl from «مَواخِر» or from the pronoun concealed in it.
«مَواخِر» is the plural of mākhira; al-makhr is cleaving; one says makharat al-safīnatu al-baḥra, i.e. the ship cleaved the sea, tamkhuruhu makhran and mukhūran. Ships are called banāt makhr and bakhr — with the mīm, the bāʾ being a substitute for it. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is the sound of the running of ships." It was said: the sound of the wind blowing hard. It was said: "banāt makhr" is said of clouds that form in summer. And imtakhartu al-rīḥa and istamkhartuhā, i.e. I faced it with my nose. In the ḥadīth: "Face the wind (istamkhirū al-rīḥ) and prepare the stones", meaning when cleaning oneself after relieving oneself. Al-mākhūr is the place where wine is sold. «ترى» here is visual only.
His saying: «ولِتَبْتَغُوا»: there are three views on it. Conjoining it to «لتأكلوا», with what is between them parenthetical — as already said — and this is the apparent view. The second: it is conjoined to an omitted cause, its implied form being "so that you may benefit from that and so that you may seek", mentioned by Ibn al-Anbārī. The third: it is attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "He did that so that you may seek". In both of these there is a strain for which there is no need.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن تَمِيدَ}: i.e. "out of aversion to its shaking", or: "lest it shake".
His saying: «وأنهاراً»: conjoined to «رَواسي», because "casting" here means creating. Ibn ʿAṭiyya's claim that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and He placed in it rivers", is not as he stated. Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated it as "and He cleaved in it rivers", which is fitting. And «سُبُلاً», i.e. "and He made smooth", or: "and He placed in it roads".

semin-durr:16-16.t:
And {وَعَلامَاتٍ}, i.e. "and He placed in it landmarks".
His saying, the Exalted: {وبالنجم}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يهتدون». The majority read it with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the jīm, in the singular. It was said: what is meant is a particular star, such as al-Jady (the Pole Star region) or al-Thurayyā (the Pleiades). It was said: rather it is a generic noun. Ibn Waththāb read it with ḍamma on both, and al-Ḥasan with ḍamma on the nūn only; some reversed the report from the two of them.
As for the reading with two ḍammas, there are two explanations of it. The more apparent: it is an explicit plural, because faʿl is pluralised on fuʿul, as in saqf / suquf and rahn / ruhun. / The second: its origin is al-nujūm, faʿl being pluralised on fuʿūl, as in fals / fulūs, then it was lightened by deleting the wāw, as they said asad / usūd and usud. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And they said for khiyām: khiyam", meaning that it is its parallel, in that they deleted the long vowel from it. Ibn ʿUṣfūr said that their saying "al-nujum" is a poetic licence, and recited:
296 - 7- إنَّ الي قَضَى بذا قاضٍ حَكَمْ ... أن تَرِدَ الماءَ إذا غابَ النُّجُمْ
(The One who decreed this is a judge who has ruled that you come down to the water when the stars (al-nujum) set.)
He means: al-nujūm [Translator's note: printed «النحوم» in the source, evidently for «النجوم»], like his saying:
296 - 8- حتى إذا ابْتَلَّتْ حَلاقِيْمُ الحُلُقْ ...
(Until, when the gullets of the throats were moistened …)
He means al-ḥulūq.
As for the reading with ḍamma and sukūn, there are two views on it. One: it is a lightening of the ḍamma form. The second: it is an independent dialectal form.
The fronting of both the prepositional phrase and the mubtadaʾ (subject) conveys restriction. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: His saying {وبالنجم هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ} departs from the course of address, the star being fronted in it and [«هم»] inserted in it, as though it were said: 'and by the star specifically, these specifically are guided' — so who are meant by them? I say: it is as though He meant Quraysh: they used to be guided by the stars in their journeys, and they had knowledge of it that others did not have, so gratitude was more incumbent on them and more binding for them." [Translator's note: the name is printed «الزمشخري» in the source, evidently for al-Zamakhsharī.]

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ}: if by «مَنْ لا يَخْلُق» is meant all that is worshipped besides Allah, then the use of «مَنْ» is clear, because the rational is given precedence over the rest, so the whole is expressed with «مَنْ»; and had «ما» been used, that too would have been permissible. If the idols are meant by it, then there are several views on applying «مَنْ» to them. The first: their treating them like beings endowed with knowledge in worshipping them and believing that they harm and benefit, like his saying:
296 - 9- بَكَيْتُ إلى سِرْبِ القَطا إذْ مَرَرْنَ بي ... فقلتُ ومِثْلي بالبكاءِ جديرُ
أسِرْبَ القَطا هل مَنْ يُعيرُ جناحَه ... لعلِّي إلى مَن قد هَوَيْتُ أطيرُ
(I wept to the flock of sand-grouse when they passed me, and I said — and one like me is worthy of weeping —: "O flock of sand-grouse, is there one (man) who will lend his wing, so that I might fly to the one I love?")
So he applied «مَنْ» to the flock when he treated them as rational beings. The second: correspondence (mushākala) between it and «مَنْ يَخْلُق». The third: restricting it to those who know, and the meaning is: if there is a disparity between one who creates and one who does not create among beings endowed with knowledge, and one who is not a creator does not deserve worship at all, then how can the worship of inanimate things be right, which are lower in rank and fallen in status below the created among beings endowed with knowledge, as in His saying {أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِهَآ} [al-Aʿrāf: 195] to the end? As for those who allow «مَنْ» to apply to non-rational beings without condition, like Quṭrub, they need no interpretation. [Translator's note: the source reads «مِنْ شرطٍ», literally "from a condition"; rendered "without condition", which the context seems to require.]
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: it is a refutation binding those who worshipped idols and the like, likening them to Allah the Exalted, and they made what is not the Creator like the Creator, so the proper form of the refutation would have been to say to them: 'Is then one who does not create like one who creates?' I say: when they made other than Allah like Allah, by calling them by His name and worshipping them, they made Him of the genus of created things and like them, so He censured them for that with His saying {أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ}."

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying, the Exalted: {يَعْلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ}: The majority read «تُسِرُّون» and «تُعْلِنون» with the tāʾ of address, and Abū Jaʿfar with the yāʾ (with dots beneath).

semin-durr:20-20.t: ʿĀṣim alone read «يَدْعُون» with yāʾ, and the rest with tāʾ (with dots above). It was also read «يُدْعَوْن» in the passive. These are all clear.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْواتٌ}: it may be a second khabar (predicate), i.e. "and they are created, and they are dead". It may be that «يُخْلَقون» and «أمواتٌ» are both a single khabar, of the type "this is sweet-sour", mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ. And it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are dead".
His saying: {غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍ}: what was said before applies to it, and it would be tawkīd (emphasis). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be that by it He intended that they are at present not alive, to remove by it the misconception that His saying «أمواتٌ» refers to what comes later, since the Exalted said: {إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَّيِّتُونَ} [al-Zumar: 30]." I say: this does not take it out of the emphasis he mentioned before that.
His saying: {أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ}: «أيَّان» is accusative by what comes after it, not by what comes before it, because it is interrogative, and it suspends (muʿallaq) «يَشْعُرون», so its clause is in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); this is the apparent view. There is another view on the verse: that «أيَّان» is an adverb for His saying {إلهكم إله وَاحِدٌ}, meaning that God is One on the Day of Resurrection, and no one will claim divinity on that day, unlike the days of this world, for in them there have been those who claimed that. On this view the sentence is complete at His saying «يَشْعُرون». But this view takes «أيَّان» out of its original function — which is either / conditional or interrogative — into pure adverbiality in the sense of "time", annexed to the clause after it, as when you say: "At the time you go, ʿAmr is departing", where "time" is accusative by "departing" and annexed to "you go".

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ جَرَمَ}: the discussion of this expression has already been given in Sūrat Hūd. The majority read with fatḥa on the hamza of «انَّ اللهَ», and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read it with kasra; there are two views on it. The more apparent: it is resumptive. The second: «لا جَرَم» is treated like an oath, so it is answered with what an oath is answered with. Some of the Arabs said: "lā jarama wa-llāhi lā fāraqtuka" (assuredly, by Allah, I will not leave you). In my view this weakens its being for an oath, since he states the oath explicitly after it, even though the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] cited it as strengthening its being treated like an oath.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّاذَآ أَنْزَلَ}: the discussion of «ماذا» has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), in the sense: what thing has your Lord sent down?" The Shaykh said: "This is not permissible according to the Basrans", meaning because it omits its accusative referent pronoun, as in "Zaydun ḍarabtu" (Zayd, I struck); the disagreement of people on this has already been given, and the correct view is that it is permissible.
What stands in place of the agent of «قيل» is the clause of His saying {مَّاذَآ أَنْزَلَ}, because it is what is said; the Basrans reject that and make what stands in its place the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun), because a clause cannot be an agent nor stand in place of an agent. The omitted agent is either the believers, or some of them, or "those who divided [the Qurʾān]" (al-muqtasimūn).
«أساطيرَ» was read in the accusative, on the estimation "He sent down tales", by way of mockery, or "you mentioned tales". The majority read it in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "what was sent down is tales", by way of mockery, or "what is mentioned is tales". Al-Zamakhsharī has a dreadful expression here that makes the hair stand on end.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَنِ اتخذي}: (أن) may be explicative (mufassira), or it may be maṣdariyya (infinitival). Some found its being explicative problematic. He said: "Because the waḥy (revelation/inspiration) here does not carry the meaning of speech, since it is an instinctive inspiration (ilhām) in which there is no speech." This is open to question, because speech for each thing is according to what befits it.
And النَّحْل (the bees) is treated as masculine and feminine, following the rule for generic nouns (asmāʾ al-ajnās). The feminine is the dialect of the Hijaz, and {أَنِ اتخذي} came in accordance with it. Ibn Waththāb read «النَحَل»; it may be an independent dialectal form, or it may be by vowel assimilation (itbāʿ).
And in {مِنَ الجبال}, «مِنْ» is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), since this is not feasible for it in every mountain and every tree. The discussion of «يَعْرِشُونَ» has preceded, together with who read it with kasra and with fatḥa, in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ذُلُلاً}: the plural of ذَلُول (tractable). It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of السُّبُل (the ways), i.e. Allah the Exalted has made them tractable, as in His words: {هُوَ الذي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأرض ذَلُولاً} [al-Mulk: 15]; or it may be a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «اسْلُكي», i.e. obedient and compliant. Both meanings are transmitted in the exegesis.
The accusative of «سُبُل» may be adverbial (ẓarfiyya), i.e. "so convey what you have eaten along the ways of your Lord", i.e. in His passages in which, by His power, He transforms the blossom and the like into honey; or it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "travel the paths which He made you understand and taught you for the making of honey". And «مِنْ» in {مِن كُلِّ الثمرات} may be partitive, or it may denote the beginning (ibtidāʾ), in the sense that it eats something that descends from the sky, resembling manna (al-taranjabīn), onto the leaves of the trees and their fruits, not that it eats the fruits themselves — and this is very far-fetched.
His words: {يَخْرُجُ مِن بُطُونِهَا}: an iltifāt (shift of person) and a statement of that; had it come in accordance with the preceding speech it would have been said: "from your bellies". The hāʾ in «فيه» refers back to «شَراب» (drink), and this is the apparent meaning; and it is said that it refers back to the Qur'an.

semin-durr:70-70.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِكَيْ لاَ}: there are two views on this lām. The first: it is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and «كي» after it is nothing but maṣdariyya (infinitival); it puts the following verb in the accusative by itself, and it together with the verb it governs is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the genitive by the lām, and the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُرَدُّ». Al-Ḥūfī said: "It is the lām of kay, and kay is for emphasis." This is open to question, because the lām is for causation while «كي» is maṣdariyya and carries no indication of causation in this situation; moreover, their governing effects differ.
The second: it is the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra).
His words: «شيئاً»: tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one word) is possible in it, for two governors precede it: «يَعْلَمَ» and «عِلْمٍ». On the view of the Basrans — and it is the preferred one — it is in the accusative by «عِلْم», and on the view of the Kufans it is in the accusative by «يَعلم». That is rejected, since had it been so, a pronoun would have been implied in the second, and it would have been said: لكيلا يعلمَ بعد عِلْمٍ إياه شيئاً.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَهُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ}: there are several views on this clause. The first: it involves the omission of the interrogative particle, its implied form being "أَفَهُمْ فيه سواءٌ" (are they then equal in it?), and its meaning is negation, i.e. they are not equal in it. The second: it is a statement of equality, meaning that what you feed and clothe your slaves with is only My provision which I have caused to flow through their hands, so they are equal in it. The third: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It stands in the place of a verb", and then he allowed two views in that verb. The first: it is in the accusative in answer to the negation, its implied form being: فما الذين فُضِّلوا برادِّي رزقِهم على ما ملكَتْ أيمانُهم فيَسْتَوُوا. The second: it is conjoined to the position of «برادّي», so it would be nominative, its implied form being: فما الذين فُضِّلوا يَرُدُّون فما يَسْتَوُوْن.
Abū Bakr read «تَجْحَدون» in the second person (khiṭāb), in keeping with His words «بعضَكم», and the rest in the third person (ghayba), in keeping with His words {فَمَا الذين فُضِّلُواْ}.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَحَفَدَةً}: there are several views on «حَفَدَة». The most apparent: it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «بنين», with the restriction of being from the spouses, and here it is explained as the children of the children (grandchildren). The second: it is a conjunction of attributes of a single thing, i.e. He made for you sons as servants, and الحَفَدَة are servants. The third: it is in the accusative by an implied «جَعَلَ»; this is according to those who explain الحَفَدَة as helpers and in-laws. An implied «جَعَلَ» was needed only because the first «جَعَلَ» is restricted by the spouses, and helpers and in-laws are not from the spouses.
And الحَفَدَة is the plural of حافِد, like خادِم and خَدَم. The exegetes have many sayings about them. Its derivation is from their saying: حَفَد يَحْفِد حَفْداً وحُفوداً وحَفَداناً, i.e. he hastened in obedience. And in the hadith: «وإليك نَسْعَى ونَحْفِدُ» (to You we strive and hasten), i.e. we hasten in obeying You. Al-Aʿshā said:
300 - 1- كَلَّفْتُ مجهولَها نُوْقاً يَمانيةً ... إذا الحُداة على أَكْسائها حَفَدُوا
(I made Yemeni she-camels cross its unknown tracts, when the camel-drivers hastened behind them.)
And another said:
300 - 2- حَفَدَ الولائدُ حولَهُنَّ وأَسْلَمَتْ ... بأكفِّهنَّ أَزِمَّةَ الأجْمالِ
(The maidservants hastened around them, and gave over with their hands the reins of the camels.)
«حَفَدَ» is also used transitively. One says: حَفَدَني فهو حافِدٌ (he served me, so he is a servant), and there was recited:
300 - 3- يَحْفِدون الضيفَ في أبياتِهمْ ... كَرَماً ذلك منهم غيرَ ذُلّْ
(They serve the guest in their tents, out of generosity on their part, not out of abasement.)
Abū ʿUbayda related that one also says «أَحْفَدَ» as a quadriliteral. Some said: "الحَفَدَة are the in-laws", and recited:
300 - 4- فلو أنَّ نفسي طاوَعَتْني لأصبحَتْ ... لها حَفَدٌ ممَّا يُعَدُّ كثيرُ
ولكنها نَفسٌ عليَّ أَبِيَّةٌ ... عَيُوفٌ لإِصهارِ اللِّئامِ قَذْوْرُ
(Had my soul obeyed me, it would have come to have many in-laws of those that are counted; but it is a soul that refuses me, disdainful and loathing of marriage ties with the base.)
And one says: سيفٌ مُحْتَفِدٌ, i.e. a sword swift in cutting. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "The root sense of الحَفْد is shortening the stride (taking quick, close steps)."
And «مِنْ» in {مِّنَ الطيبات} is partitive.

semin-durr:73-73.t:
The words of the Exalted: {شَيْئاً}: there are three views on it. The first: it is in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. it does not possess for them any possessing, i.e. anything of possession. The second: it is a badal (substitute) of «رِزْقاً», i.e. it does not possess anything for them. This is not informative, since it is known that provision is one of the things. This is supported by the fact that the badal comes for one of two meanings: clarification or emphasis, and here there is no clarification, because it is more general, nor emphasis. The third: it is in the accusative by «رِزْقاً», on the basis that it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), and the ism maṣdar governs as the maṣdar governs — with disagreement about that.
Makkī transmitted that the ism maṣdar does not govern according to the Basrans except in poetry. I say: the transmitters have differed about the Basrans: some transmitted the prohibition and some transmitted the permissibility. Al-Fārisī mentioned its being in the accusative by «رِزْقاً», as has preceded. Ibn al-Ṭarāwa rebutted him on the grounds that الرِّزْق is a noun for the thing provided, like الرَّعْي (pasture) and الطَّحْن (flour). Ibn al-Ṭarāwa was rebutted in turn on the grounds that الرِّزْق with kasra is also a maṣdar, and that has been heard in it. I say: the apparent sense of this is that it is a maṣdar in itself, not an ism maṣdar.
And His words: {مِّنَ السماوات}: there are three views on it. The first: it is attached to «يملك», and that is on the first two parsings of the accusative of «شيئاً». The second: it is attached to something omitted, as a ṣifa (adjective) of «رزقاً». The third: it is attached to «رِزْقاً» itself, if we make it a maṣdar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said — after mentioning the governing of the maṣdar with tanwīn: "The maṣdar governs when in iḍāfa (annexation) by agreement, because it is in the sense of separation (i.e. the annexation is notionally dissolved); and it does not govern when the alif and lām enter it, because it has then gone deep into the state of nouns and become remote from verbality; the notional separation in the annexation is what made its governing acceptable. It has come governing with the alif and lām in the words of the poet:
300 - 5- ضعيفُ النكايةِ أعداءَه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Weak in inflicting harm on his enemies …)
[And his words]:
300 - 6-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فلم أَنْكِلْ عن الضَرْبِ مِسْمَعا
(… and I did not shrink from striking Misma.)"
The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for his saying 'by agreement': if he meant of the Basrans, it is correct; and if he meant of the grammarians, it is not correct, since some of them held that it does not govern, and if an accusative or nominative is found after it, they imply a governor for it. As for his saying 'in the sense of separation', it is not so, lest its annexation be non-genuine (ghayr maḥḍa), as Ibn al-Ṭarāwa and Ibn Barhān held; and their position is unsound, because this maṣdar has been qualified by an adjective and emphasised with a definite word. And his saying 'it does not govern' to the end, he contradicted by his saying 'it has come governing' to the end."
I say: the most that this amounts to is that he inclined to positions held by others. As for the contradiction, it is not valid, because he meant first that it does not govern in ordinary usage (al-saʿa), and second that it has come governing under poetic necessity (al-ḍarūra); that is why he restricted it, saying: "in the words of the poet".
His words: {وَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ}: two views are possible in the clause: conjunction to the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما», or a statement about them negating the capacity by way of a new sentence (istiʾnāf). The pronoun referring back to «ما» would then have been made plural with regard to its meaning, since what is meant by it is their gods. And it is possible that the pronoun refers back to the worshippers.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَمَن رَّزَقْنَاهُ}: «مَنْ» here may be a relative (mawṣūla), or it may be qualified (mawṣūfa, an indefinite noun described by the following clause). Al-Zamakhsharī chose the latter, saying: "It is as though it were said: and a free man whom We provided, so as to correspond to عَبْداً." Its position is accusative, conjoined to «عبداً». The discussion of the "parable" (al-mathal) coming after «ضَرَبَ» has preceded.
His words: {سِرّاً وَجَهْراً}: it may be in the accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. a spending of secrecy and openness; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His words: {هَلْ يَسْتَوُونَ}: the pronoun was made plural even though two preceded it only because what is meant is the genus of slaves and free men indicated by "a slave" and by "the one whom We provided". It is also said: it refers to the rich and the poor, likewise indicated by them. And it is said: with regard to the meaning of «مَنْ», for its meaning is plural; He observed its meaning after having observed its wording.
His words: {وَأَنْتُمْ لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ} [al-Naḥl: 74]: the object of knowing was omitted, for brevity (ikhtiṣār) or by restriction (iqtiṣār).

semin-durr:76-76.t:
And الكَلّ: the heavy one; and الكَلّ: dependants, its plural being كُلُول. And الكَلّ: one who has neither child nor parent; and الكَلّ is also the orphan, so called because of his heaviness on his guardian. The poet said:
300 - 7- أَكُولٌ لِمالِ الكَلِّ قبل شبابِه ... إذا كان عَظْمُ الكَلِّ غيرَ شديدِ
(A devourer of the orphan's wealth before he comes of age, while the orphan's bone is not yet strong.)
His words: {أَيْنَمَا يُوَجِّههُّ لاَ يَأْتِ}: a condition and its apodosis (jawāb). Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn Waththāb and ʿAlqama read «يُوَجِّهْ» with a single sukūn-bearing hāʾ, for the jussive. There are two views on its fāʿil (agent). The first: it is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, and its object is omitted, its implied form being as in the reading of the majority. The second: it is the pronoun of the mute one (al-abkam), and «يُوَجِّه» is intransitive in the sense of تَوَجَّه (he turns his face); one says وَجَّه and تَوَجَّه with the same meaning.
ʿAlqama also, and Ṭalḥa, read it likewise, except with ḍamma on the hāʾ, and there are several views on it. The first: «أينما» here is not conditional, and «يُوَجِّهُ» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. أينما هو يُوَجِّهُ, i.e. Allah the Exalted, and the object is also omitted; and the yāʾ was dropped from {لاَ يَأْتِ} for lightness, as it was dropped in His words {يَوْمَ يَأْتِ} [Hūd: 106] and {إِذَا يَسْرِ} [al-Fajr: 4]. This was rejected on the grounds that «أينما» is only either conditional or interrogative, and the interrogative is not fitting here. The second: the final radical of the word was dropped for lightness because of the doubling, and this hāʾ is the hāʾ of the pronoun, so the jussive did not affect it. Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī mentioned these two views.
The third: «أينما» was left without governing effect, by analogy with «إذا», because of the kinship between them in conditionality, just as «إذا» was treated by analogy with it in taking the jussive in the very same contexts; and the yāʾ was dropped from «يَأْتِ» for lightness, or as a jussive by notional assumption (ʿalā al-tawahhum), and «يُوَجِّهُ» is intransitive in the sense of يَتَوَجَّه, as has preceded.
[And ʿAbd Allāh also read it.] And Abū Ḥātim said — having related this reading: "This is weak, because the jussive is necessary", and it is as though he did not know how to account for it.
ʿAlqama and Ṭalḥa read «يُوَجَّهْ» with a single sukūn-bearing hāʾ for the jussive, the verb being passive; and it is clear.
Ibn Masʿūd also read «تُوَجِّهْه», like the majority, except with the tāʾ of address, and in it there is an iltifāt (shift of person).
And in the speech there is an omission, namely the omission of the counterpart to His words {أَحَدُهُمَآ أَبْكَمُ}, as though it were said: "and the other is articulate, managing his wealth, and he is light on his master; wherever he sends him, he brings good." What indicates that is His words: {هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هُوَ وَمَن يَأْمُرُ بالعدل}.
Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted that it was read «أينما تَوَجَّهَ» as a past verb, its fāʿil being the pronoun of the mute one.
And His words: {وَمَن يَأْمُرُ}: the preponderant view is that it is nominative, conjoined to the nominative pronoun in «يَسْتوي», this being made permissible by the separation with the pronoun (هو). The accusative as an object of accompaniment (al-maʿiyya) is the weaker view. {وَهُوَ على صِرَاطٍ}: the clause is either resumptive (istiʾnāf) or a ḥāl.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَحْمِلُواْ}: there are three views on this lām. The first: it is the jussive lām of command, in the sense of something decreed against them and the humiliation that is their due; on this view the sentence is complete at His saying «الأوَّلين», and then their being commanded to that begins anew. The second: it is the lām of outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba), i.e. that was the outcome of their saying, because they did not say «أساطير» in order to bear [burdens]; so it is like His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], and his saying:
297 - 0- لِدُوا للموتِ وابْنُوا للخرابِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Give birth for death and build for ruin …)
The third: it is causal, and there are two views on it. One: it is a figurative cause. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The lām is causal without being a purpose, as when you say: I left the town for fear of evil." The second: it is a real cause. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said — after reporting the view of the lām of outcome —: "It may be an explicit lām of kay (purpose), in the sense: He decreed this for such-and-such" — end of quotation. But he did not attach it to «قالوا»; he only estimated for it the cause of «كيلا», namely "He decreed this"; whereas on al-Zamakhsharī's view it is attached to «قالوا», because it is not for a real cause. «كاملةً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying: {وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ}: there are two views on it. One: «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida), which is the view of al-Akhfash, i.e. "and the burdens of those who", in the sense "and the like of the burdens of", as in his ﷺ saying: "Upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it." The second: it is not redundant and is partitive, i.e. "and some of the burdens of those who". Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated an omitted object of which this is the naʿt (adjective), i.e. "and burdens from the burdens of"; and the omission of "the like of" is also necessary.
Al-Wāḥidī rejected «مِنْ» being partitive. He said: "Because it entails lightening the burdens of the followers, which is not permissible, given his saying, upon him be peace: 'without anything being diminished from their burdens'; rather it is for the genus, i.e. so that they bear [something] of the genus of the followers' burdens." The Shaykh said: "The one that is for clarifying the genus is not estimated in this way; it is only estimated as: and the burdens which are the burdens of those who; so in meaning it is like al-Akhfash's view, even though they differ in the estimation."
His saying: {بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ}: a ḥāl, and there are two views on the one it describes. One: it is the object of «يُضِلُّونهم», i.e. they lead astray those who do not know that they are misguided; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: it is the agent, and this was preferred because it is the one being spoken about. The discussion of the i'rab of the like of «ساءَ ما يَزِرون» has already been given, and that it may be treated like biʾsa.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّنَ القواعد}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. from the direction of the foundations; i.e. Allah's command and His punishment came.
His saying: {مِن فَوْقِهِمْ}: it may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خَرَّ», with «مِنْ» for the beginning of the extent; or it may / be attached to an omitted [word] on the basis that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السقف», and it is an emphasising ḥāl, since a roof is not beneath them. A group said: His saying «مِنْ تحتِهم» is not emphasis, because the Arabs say "a roof fell in on us, and a wall fell on us" when one owns it even if it did not fall on him; so He brought His saying «من فوقهم» to exclude this usage in the speech of the Arabs, i.e. it fell upon them while they were under it, and they perished. [Translator's note: the source has «مِنْ تحتِهم» here, evidently for «مِن فوقهم»; translated as written.] This is a meaning of little value; the view of emphasis is clearer than it.
The majority read «بُنْيانِهم». A group read «بِنْيَتَهُمْ», and a group — among them Abū Jaʿfar — «بَيْتهم», and al-Ḍaḥḥāk «بُيوتهم».
The majority also read «السَّقْفُ» in the singular. A group read it with fatḥa on the sīn and ḍamma on the qāf, on the pattern of ʿaḍud; it is a dialectal form of al-saqf, and perhaps it is lightened from the ḍamma form, and the derived form came to be used more because of its lightness, like Tamīm's saying "rajl" while they do not say "rajul". [Translator's note: the logic of the sentence suggests the vowelling is reversed here (saqf lightened from saquf); translated as written.] Al-Aʿraj read «السُّقُف» with two ḍammas, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī with ḍamma on the sīn and sukūn on the qāf; the like of this has already been given in the reading of {وبالنجم هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ} [al-Naḥl: 16].

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَيْنَ شُرَكَآئِيَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The majority read «شركائي» with the long vowel (mamdūd). A group read the yāʾ of the speaker with sukūn, so it is dropped in continuous recitation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Bazzī read it — with a disagreement in the transmission from him — shortened (maqṣūr), with fatḥa on the yāʾ. A group rejected this reading and claimed that it is not to be adopted, because shortening a long-vowelled word is permissible only as poetic licence. Abū Shāma expressed astonishment at Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī for mentioning it in his book despite its weakness while leaving out well-known, clear readings.
I say: the shortening of the one in al-Qaṣaṣ has also been narrated from Ibn Kathīr, and the shortening of «ورائي» in Maryam has also been narrated from him, and Qunbul also narrated from him the shortening of {أَن رَّآهُ استغنى} [verse 7] in al-ʿAlaq. So he has been reported to shorten some long-vowelled words, and it is not far-fetched that this be reported from him here. In sum, shortening a long-vowelled word is weak — more than one scholar has said so — but it does not reach the level of poetic licence.
His saying: «تُشَاقُّون»: Nāfiʿ read it with kasra on the nūn, unstressed; the origin is tushāqqūnī, and he dropped it [the yāʾ], making do with the kasra in its place. The rest read it with fatḥa, unstressed, and its object is omitted, i.e. "you oppose the believers" or "you oppose Allah", as shown by the first reading. Abū Ḥātim declared this reading weak — I mean Nāfiʿ's reading. A group read it with doubling (tashdīd) and kasra; the origin is tushāqqūnanī, and it was assimilated. The details of this have already been given in {أتحاجواني} [al-Anʿām: 80] and {فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ} [al-Ḥijr: 54], and it will come in His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ أَفَغَيْرَ الله تأمروني} [al-Zumar: 64].
His saying: «اليومَ»: accusative by «الخِزْي», the maṣdar (verbal noun) governing although it has al-. It was said: it is accusative by the [notion of] being-established in «على الكافرين», except that this involves separating the governor from what it governs by the conjoined element; that was overlooked because they allow latitude with adverbs.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ}: the relative noun may be in the position of a genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it, or as a badal (substitute) from it, or [Translator's note: printed «أبو», evidently for «أو»] as an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it; or it may be accusative by way of censure, or nominative by way of it, or nominative by way of it [Translator's note: the phrase "or nominative by way of it" is repeated in the source], or nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being His saying {فَأَلْقَوُاْ السلم}, with the fāʾ redundant in the khabar; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. This only works on the opinion of al-Akhfash, who allows the redundancy of the fāʾ in the khabar without restriction, as in "Zaydun fa-qāma", i.e. "qāma". It should not be imagined that this fāʾ is the one that comes with a relative noun carrying the sense of a condition, because if this verb were stated explicitly with a conditional particle, the fāʾ could not enter on it, so what merely carries its sense is more deserving of being barred; so the Shaykh said, and it is evident. On the views given above, except the last view, «الذين» and its ṣila (relative clause) are included in what is said (al-maqūl); on the last view it is not included in it.
Ḥamza read «يَتَوَفَّاهُمْ» in both places with yāʾ, and the rest with tāʾ (with dots above); both are clear from what was said on His saying {فَنَادَتْهُ الملائكة} [Āl ʿImrān: 39] / «فناداه». A group read with the assimilation of one of the two tāʾs into the other; in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is «تَوَفَّاهم» with a single tāʾ, which can bear reading with doubling by assimilation, or without doubling by dropping one of the two tāʾs.
{ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «تَتَوَفَّاهم». And «تَتَوَفَّاهم» may be future in its proper sense if the saying takes place in this world, or past by way of narrating a past situation (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl) if it takes place on the Day of Resurrection.
His saying: «فَأَلْقَوا»: several views are possible. The first: it is the khabar of the relative noun, and its unsoundness has already been given. The second: it is conjoined to {قَالَ الذين}. The third: it is resumptive, and the sentence is complete [Translator's note: printed «قم», evidently for «قد»] at His saying «أنفسِهم»; then with His saying «فألْقَوا» He returned to narrating the speech of the idolaters on the Day of Resurrection; on this view His saying {قَالَ الذين أُوتُواْ العلم} up to His saying «أنفسهم» is a parenthetical clause. The fourth: it is conjoined to «تَتَوفَّاهم», as Abū al-Baqāʾ said; this only works on «تَتَوفَّاهم» having the sense of the past, and for that reason Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned nothing else for «تَتَوفَّاهم».
His saying: {مَا كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is an explanation of the submission (al-salam) that they offered, because it has the sense of speech, as shown by the other verse: {فَألْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ القول} [al-Naḥl: 86]; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. Had he said "it reports what has the sense of speech", it would have agreed better with the school of the Kufans. The second: «ما كنَّا» is accusative by an implied verb of saying, that verb being accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "they offered submission, saying that". / {مِن سواء} is the object of «نعمل», with «مِنْ» added to it [Translator's note: the Quranic text reads «مِن سُوءٍ»; printed here as «مِن سواء»]; and «بلى» is the answer to «ما كنَّا», so it is an affirmation of it.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَبِئْسَ}: this is the lām of emphasis; it entered on the past verb only because of its inflexibility (jumūd) and its closeness to nouns. The one specified for censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. Hell.

semin-durr:77-77.t: The words of the Exalted: {أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ}: i.e. "or a matter"; the pronoun is for the matter, and the implied form is: "or the matter of the Hour is nearer than the twinkling of the eye."

semin-durr:78-78.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئاً}: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «أَخْرجكم», i.e. He brought you out not knowing. And «شيئاً» is either a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. anything of knowledge, or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Knowledge here is recognition (al-ʿirfān). The discussion of «أمَّهاتكم» has preceded in al-Nisāʾ.
His words: «وَجَعَلَ»: it may be conjoined to «أَخْرجكم», and so be included in what is stated about the mubtadaʾ (subject); and it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
And الأَفْئِدَة is the plural of «فؤاد» (heart), and it has preceded. Al-Rāzī said: "It was given a plural of paucity only because most people are occupied with beastly acts, so it is as though they have no heart." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is one of the plurals used for both paucity and abundance, for which nothing other than the plural of paucity has been heard, like «شُسُوع» (sandal-thongs), which is for abundance but is used for paucity, nothing other than شُسُوع having been heard." So he said, and this is open to question: «أَشْسَاع» has been heard from them, so he ought to have said: شُسُوع predominated.

semin-durr:79-79.t: The words of the Exalted: {مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ}: the clause may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «مُسَخَّراتٍ», or it may be a ḥāl of «الطير», or it may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa).

semin-durr:80-80.t:
The words of the Exalted: {سَكَناً}: it may be a first object, on the basis that الجَعْل (making) means transforming (taṣyīr), the second object being one of the two prepositional phrases before it. And الجَعْل may be in the sense of creating, so it takes a single object. السَّكَن was made singular only because it means "what you dwell in" — Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. It may also be said that it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) — and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this — so its being singular is clear. However, the Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] [Translator's note: a verb appears to be missing in the source here; the sense is evidently "rejected"] its being a maṣdar, and did not mention the reason for the rejection; it is as though he relied on the statement of the lexicographers that «السَّكَن» is of the pattern faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), like القَبَض and النَّقَض in the sense of the thing seized and the thing demolished. Al-Farrāʾ recited:
300 - 8- جاء الشتاءُ ولَمَّا أتخِذْ سَكَناً ... يا ويحَ نفسي مِنْ حَفْرِ القراميصِ
(Winter has come and I have not yet taken a dwelling; woe to me for digging burrows!)
His words: {يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكُمْ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and the rest with sukūn; they are two dialectal forms with one meaning, like النَّهْر and النَّهَر. Some claimed that the original is the fatḥa, and the sukūn is a lightening because of the guttural letter, like الشَّعْر for الشَّعَر.
His words: {أَثَاثاً}: there are two views on it. The first: it is in the accusative, conjoined to «بُيوتاً», i.e. "and He made for you from their wool furnishings"; on this view He has conjoined a genitive to a genitive and an accusative to an accusative, and there is then no separation between the conjunction and the conjoined word. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "There is a separation between it and the conjunction by the preposition and its genitive noun, namely His words {وَمِنْ أَصْوَافِهَا}; and it is not an ugly separation as was claimed in al-Īḍāḥ, because the prepositional phrase is an object, and placing one object before another is regular." This is open to question, given what you have learned, that it is a conjunction of a genitive to its like and an accusative to its like.
The second: it is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and He will have conjoined a genitive to its like, the implied form being: "And He made for you from the hides of the cattle and from their wool, their fur and their hair houses, in the state of being furnishings", so He separated the two conjoined elements with the object. But the meaning is not according to this; it is only according to the first.
And His words: {كَلَمْحِ البصر} [al-Naḥl: 77]: اللَّمْح is the maṣdar of لَمَحَ يَلْمَح لَمْحاً ولَمَحاناً, i.e. he looked quickly. It is said that its origin is from the flashing (lamḥ) of lightning; and their saying «لأُرِيَنَّك لَمْحاً باصراً» (I will surely show you a clear glimpse), i.e. a plain matter.
And His words: {فِي جَوِّ السمآء} [al-Naḥl: 79]: الجَوّ is the air, which is what is between the sky and the earth. He said:
300 - 9- فلستَ لإِنْسيٍّ ولكن لِمَلأَكٍ ... تَنَزَّلَ مِنْ جَوِّ السماء يَصُوبُ
(You are not of a human but of an angel who descended from the expanse of the sky, swooping down.)
It is also said: الجَوّ is what adjoins the earth in the direction of height, and اللُّوح and السُّكاك are farther than it.
And His words: «ظَعْنِكم» is the maṣdar of ظَعَن, i.e. he set out on a journey. And الظَّعِيْنَة is the howdah with a woman in it — otherwise it is a litter (maḥmal) — then it became frequent until the woman herself was called ظَعينة.
The lexicographers said: الأصواف (wool) is for sheep, الأَوْبار (fur) for camels, and الشَّعْر (hair) for goats. And الأَثاث is household goods when they are many. Its origin is from أثَّ الشعرُ والنَّباتُ, when hair and plants become dense and plentiful. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
301 - 0- وفَرْعٍ يُغْشَي المَتْنَ أسودَ فاحمٍ ... أثيثٍِ كقِنْوِ النخلةِ المُتَعَثْكِلِ
(And long tresses covering the back, jet black, thick, like the laden cluster of a date-palm.)
And نساء أَثائِث, i.e. full-fleshed women, as though they had furnishings on them; and تَأَثَّث فلانٌ: his furnishings became many. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "الأثاث is what is new of the house's furnishings, and الخُرْثِيّ is what is old of them", and recited:
301 - 1- تقادَم العهدُ مِنْ أُمِّ الوليد بنا ... دَهْراً وصار أثاثُ البيتِ خُرْثِيَّا
(Our time with Umm al-Walīd has grown long ago, and the house's furnishings have become worn-out junk.)
Does it have a singular from its own root? Al-Farrāʾ said: No. Abū Zayd said: "Its singular is أَثاثَة, and its plural of paucity is أثِثَّة, like بَتات and أَبِتَّة." The Shaykh said: "And of abundance, أَثَث." This is open to question, because the doubled pattern faʿāl necessarily has its plural on afʿila for both paucity and abundance, and it is not pluralised on fuʿul except in two words that are anomalous, namely عُنُن and حُجُج, plurals of عِنان and حِجاج; and the grammarians have stipulated that analogy on them is prohibited, so زِمام and زُمُم is not permitted, but rather أَزِمَّة. [Translator's note: the source writes «أَثَث», whereas the pattern under discussion is fuʿul («أُثُث»); translated as written.] Al-Khalīl said: "الأَثاث and المَتاع are one thing, and they were joined together because their wordings differ, as in his words:
301 - 2-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
وأَلْفَى قولَها كَذِباً ومَيْنا
(… and he found her words to be falsehood and lying.)
[And his words]:
301 - 3-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . أتى مِنْ دونِها النَّأْيُ والبُعْدُ
(… between him and her came remoteness and distance.)"

semin-durr:81-81.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَكْنَاناً}: the plural of «كِنّ», which is what protects from wind and rain; in a mountain it is the cave.
His words: {تَقِيكُمُ الحر}: it is said that the conjoined word was omitted because the meaning is understood, i.e. "and the cold", as in his words:
301 - 4- كأنَّ الحصى مِنْ خلفِها وأمامِها ... إذا نَجَلَتْه رِجْلُها حَذْفُ أَعْسرا
(As though the pebbles behind her and before her, when her foot kicks them up, were the throw of a left-handed man.)
i.e. "and her forefoot". It is also said: there is no need for that, because their lands are hot. Al-Zajjāj said: "He confined Himself to mentioning heat, because what protects from it protects from the cold." This is open to question, because of the need for much additional covering to protect from the cold.
His words: {كَذَلِكَ يُتِمُّ}: i.e. like that previous completing, He completes His blessing upon you in the future. Ibn ʿAbbās read «تَتِمُّ» with fatḥa on the first tāʾ, with «نِعْمَتُه» in the nominative as fāʿil (agent). He also read «نِعَمه», the plural of «نعمة», annexed to the pronoun of Allah the Exalted. And from him: {لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ} with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the lām, the imperfect of «سَلِم» from السَّلامة (safety); and this suits His words {تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ}, for what is meant by it is the coats of mail worn in war.

semin-durr:82-82.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ}: it may be a past verb, in which case it is an iltifāt (shift of person) from the preceding address; or it may be an imperfect, the original being تَتَوَلَّوا with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped, as in {تَنَزَّلُ} [al-Qadr: 4] and {تَذَكَّرُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 152]; on this view there is no iltifāt, rather it continues the preceding address.
His words: {فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ البلاغ}: this is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); in reality the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then you are excused", and this is only by putting the cause in place of the effect; that is because his conveying is the cause of his being excused, so the cause was put in place of the effect.

semin-durr:83-83.t: The words of the Exalted: {ثُمَّ يُنكِرُونَهَا}: «ثُمَّ» was brought here to indicate that their denial is something remote after knowledge has been attained, because one who knows the blessing ought to acknowledge it, not deny it.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is in the accusative by an implied "remember" (اذكر). The second: by an implied «خَوِّفْهم» (warn them). The third: its implied form is: "and on the day We raise up, they will fall into a grave matter." The fourth: it is conjoined to an omitted adverb of time, i.e. "they deny it today and on the day We raise up."
His words: {ثُمَّ لاَ يُؤْذَنُ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of this «ثم»? I say: its meaning is that, after the testimony of the prophets, they are afflicted with something more overwhelming than it, namely that they are prevented from speaking, so they are not permitted to offer an excuse or to produce an argument." End of quote. The object of the permission is omitted, i.e. they are not permitted to speak, as al-Zamakhsharī said, or: to return to the world.
His words: {وَلاَ هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ}: i.e. their cause of reproach (ʿutbā) is not removed, which is that for which they are reproached and blamed. One says اسْتَعْتَبْتُ فلاناً in the sense of أَعْتَبْتُه, i.e. I removed his cause of reproach; and istafʿala in the sense of afʿala is not objectionable: they said اسْتَدْنَيْتُ فلاناً and أَدْنَيْتُه with one meaning (I brought him near). It is also said: the sīn has its usual sense of seeking, and its meaning is that they are not asked to turn back from what they were upon in the world; so this is an istiʿtāb meaning seeking their ʿutbā (their making amends). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Nor are they asked to give satisfaction, i.e. it is not said to them: satisfy your Lord, because the Hereafter is not an abode of deeds." Further explanation of this will come, Allah willing, in Sūrat Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda, because it is more fitting there owing to the readers' disagreement over it.

semin-durr:85-85.t: The words of the Exalted: {فَلاَ يُخَفَّفُ}: this fāʾ and what is within its scope are the answer (jawāb) of «إذا», and a mubtadaʾ (subject) must be implied before this fāʾ, i.e. "then it is not lightened", because whenever the answer of «إذا» is an imperfect it does not need a fāʾ, whether affirmative, as in the words of the Exalted: {وَإِذَا تتلى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ تَعْرِفُ} [al-Ḥajj: 72], or negated, as in: «إذا جاء زيدٌ لا يكرُمك» (when Zayd comes he will not honour you).

semin-durr:87-87.t: The words of the Exalted: {السلم}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the sīn and the lām, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read it with sukūn on the lām, and Mujāhid with ḍamma on the sīn and the lām. It is as though it were the plural of «سَلام», like قَذَال and قُذُل. And السَّلام and السَّلَم are one thing; the discussion of them has preceded in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.

semin-durr:88-88.t: The words of the Exalted: {الذين كَفَرُواْ}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being «زِدْناهم», and this is clear. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed {الذين كَفَرُواْ} to be a badal (substitute) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يَفْتَرُوْن», with «زِدْناهم» resumptive. And {الذين كَفَرُواْ} may be in the accusative by way of censure (al-dhamm), or in the nominative by way of it, in which case the governor of the accusative and the mubtadaʾ are necessarily implied.

semin-durr:89-89.t:
The words of the Exalted: {تِبْيَاناً}: it may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and no maṣdars have come on this pattern except two words: this and تِلْقاء; among nouns there are many, such as التِّمْساح (crocodile) and التِّمْثال (statue). As for maṣdars, their regular form is with fatḥa on the first letter, indicating intensity, like التِّطواف and التِّجْوال. [Translator's note: the words are printed in the source with kasra on the first letter, although the statement concerns fatḥa (التَّطواف, التَّجْوال); kept as printed.] Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "التِّبْيان is a noun and not a maṣdar", and the grammarians hold the contrary.
His words: «للمُسْلمين» is attached to «بُشْرَى», and in terms of meaning it is attached to {وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً} as well. Whether this may be a case of tanāzuʿ (two or more governors contending for one word) is open to question, since it would require separating the maṣdar from the word it governs by the conjoined word when you make other than the third govern; so reflect on it. The analogy of the position of those who allow tanāzuʿ with the verb of wonder (fiʿl al-taʿajjub) and require making the second govern, so that separation does not result, is that they should allow this in this situation.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {خَيْراً}: «خيراً»: the majority read it in the accusative, i.e. "He sent down good". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did you say: why [Translator's note: the words «لِمَ قلتَ: لِمَ» are duplicated in the source] did He put the first in the nominative and this one in the accusative? I say: to distinguish between the answer of the one who acknowledges and the answer of the one who denies." He means that when these were asked they did not hesitate, and they fitted the answer to the question clearly and openly, as the object of the sending down, so they said: "good"; while those others turned the answer away from the question and said: "it is the tales of the ancients", and it is not at all something sent down.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «خيرٌ» in the nominative, i.e. "what was sent down is good"; this supports making «ذا» a relative noun, which is better because the answer then corresponds to its question, although the reverse is permissible; its verification has already been given in al-Baqara.
His saying: {لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ فِي هذه الدنيا حَسَنَةٌ}: several views are possible for this clause. The first: it is cut off from what precedes it, a resumptive statement of that. The second: it is a badal (substitute) from «خيراً». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a substitute from «خيراً», a report of the words of those who are God-fearing, i.e. they said this statement; so He first named it 'good', then reported it." The third: this clause is an explanation of His saying «خيراً»; that is, the "good" is the revelation that Allah sent down, in which [it is stated that] whoever does good in this world through obedience has good in this world and good in the Hereafter.
His saying: {فِي هذه الدنيا}: the apparent view is that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَحْسَنوا», i.e. they performed good in the abode of this world. It may be attached to an omitted [word] on the basis that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حَسَنَة», since had it been placed after it, it would have been a naʿt (adjective) of it; its being attached to the word itself is weak because it precedes it.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ}: it may be the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ), in which case the three views apply to it: its being nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the preceding clause as its khabar (predicate); or its being nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ; or its being nominative as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, which is the weakest of them — the verification of this has already been given. {جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ} may also be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, not in the way just mentioned; rather the one specified [for praise] is omitted, its implied form being: "and excellent indeed is the abode of the God-fearing — their abode, which is gardens". Al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as: "and excellent indeed is the abode of the God-fearing — the abode of the Hereafter". It may be a mubtadaʾ with the khabar being the clause of His saying «يَدْخلونها»; and the khabar may be implied, its implied form being "theirs are gardens of ʿAdn", as indicated by His saying {لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ فِي هذه الدنيا حَسَنَةٌ}.
The majority read «جناتُ» in the nominative, as described. Zayd ibn Thābit and al-Sulamī read «جناتِ» in the accusative, by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb) with an implied verb, its implied form being "they enter gardens of ʿAdn — they enter them"; this strengthens [the view] that «جنات» is a mubtadaʾ and «يَدْخلونها» the khabar in the reading of the majority.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ولَنِعْمَةُ دارِ» with the feminine tāʾ, nominative as a mubtadaʾ, «دارِ» genitive by annexation, and «جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ» the khabar. «يَدْخُلونها» in all of this is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), except when we make it the khabar of {جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ}.
Nāfiʿ read in one transmission «يُدْخَلُونها» with yāʾ (dots beneath), in the passive, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān «تَدْخُلونها» with the tāʾ of address, in the active.
His saying: «تَجْري»: it may be accusative as a ḥāl from «جنات», as Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, or in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات», as al-Ḥawfī said. The two views are based on the opinion about «عَدْن»: is it definite because it is a proper name, or indefinite? The one who says ḥāl considered the first, and the one who says naʿt considered the second.
His saying: {لَهُمْ فِيهَا مَا يَشَآؤونَ}: the discussion of this clause is like the discussion of the clause before it, and the khabar is either «لهم» or «فيها».
His saying: «كذلك»: the kāf is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun), or a naʿt [Translator's note: printed «نهتٌ», evidently for «نعتٌ»] of an implied maṣdar, or in the position of a nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is thus". {يَجْزِي الله المتقين} is resumptive.
And {
[Translator's note: the entry breaks off here in the source; the continuation appears at the start of the next entry (verse 32).]

semin-durr:32-32.t:
And {الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ} admits what we mentioned earlier. If we make «يقولون» the khabar (predicate), an omitted referent pronoun is necessary, i.e. "they say to them"; and if we do not make it the khabar, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الملائكة», / so «طيبين» is a ḥāl from the object and «يقولون» a ḥāl from the agent. It may be a concurrent ḥāl if the saying takes place in this world, and an anticipated ḥāl (muqaddara) if it takes place in the Hereafter.
«ما» in «بما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), or in the sense of «الذي», with the referent pronoun omitted.

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمُ الملائكة}: it has already been given at the end of al-Anʿām that the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with yāʾ (dots beneath), and the rest read it with tāʾ (dots above); both are clear, since the feminine is figurative.

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَصَابَهُمْ}: conjoined to {فَعَلَ الذين}, and what is between them is parenthetical.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَنِ اعبدوا الله}: «أَنْ» may be explicative (tafsīriyya), because sending [a messenger] implies speech; or maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "We sent him with [the message] that you worship".
His saying: {مَّنْ هَدَى} and {مَّنْ حَقَّتْ}: it may be a relative noun, or an indefinite noun qualified by a description; on both estimations the referent pronoun is omitted from the first.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
The majority read {إِن تَحْرِصْ} with kasra on the rāʾ, the imperfect of ḥaraṣa with fatḥa, which is the most eloquent dialect, the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Al-Ḥasan and Abū Ḥaywa read «تَحْرَصُ» with fatḥa on the rāʾ, the imperfect of ḥariṣa with kasra, which is the dialect of some of them; and likewise al-Nakhaʿī, except that he added a wāw before «إنْ» and read {وَإنْ تَحْرَصْ}.
His saying: {لاَ يَهْدِي}: the Kufans read «يَهْدِي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the dāl. This reading admits two views. One: the agent is a pronoun referring back to Allah, i.e. "Allah does not guide whom He leads astray", so «مَنْ» is the object of «يَهْدِي»; this is supported by the reading of Ubayy «فإنَّ اللهَ لا هاديَ لِمَنْ يُضِلُّ، ولِمَنْ أضلَّ» ("for Allah — there is no guide for whom He leads astray, and for whom He has led astray"), and by its being in the sense of His saying: {مَن يُضْلِلِ الله فَلاَ هَادِيَ لَهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 186].
The second: the relative noun is the agent, i.e. "those who are led astray are not guided", «يَهْدِي» coming in the sense of «يهتدي» (is guided). One says: hadāhu fa-hadā, i.e. he guided him and he was guided (ihtadā). This view is supported by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «يَهْدِي» with doubling of the dāl with kasra, so he assimilated. Some reported in this reading kasra on the hāʾ by vowel harmony (itbāʿ), and its verification has already been given in Yūnus. The referent pronoun to «مَنْ» is omitted: {مَن يُضِلُّ}, i.e. the one whom Allah leads astray.
The rest read «لا يُهْدَى» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the dāl, in the passive, «مَنْ» standing in place of its agent, and its referent pronoun is also omitted.
Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «مَنْ» to be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with «لا يَهْدِي» as its khabar (predicate), meaning placed before it. This is a mistake, because whenever the khabar is a verb with a latent (mustatir) pronoun as its agent, it must come after [the mubtadaʾ], as in "Zaydun lā yaḍribu" (Zayd does not strike); had you put it first, it would be confused with the agent.
It was also read «لا يُهْدِيْ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the dāl. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is weak." The Shaykh said: "If it is established that «هَدَى» is intransitive in the sense of «اهتدى», it is not weak, because he has put the transitivising hamza on the intransitive verb, so the meaning is: whoever Allah has led astray is not made guided."
His saying: «ومالهم»: it was construed according to the meaning of «مَنْ», and for that reason it is plural.
It was also read «مَنْ يَضِلُّ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, from ḍalla, i.e. He does not guide one who has gone astray of himself.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَقْسَمُواْ}: its apparent sense is that it is a resumptive statement; al-Zamakhsharī made it conjoined to «وقال الذين أشركوا», as an indication that they are two enormous acts of disbelief. His saying: {وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقّاً}: these two are accusative as an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "He promised that, and it is true, truly". It was said: «حقاً» is a naʿt (adjective) of «وَعْد», the implied form being: "Yes, He will resurrect them — He promised that." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read {وَعْدٌ عَلَيْهِ حَقٌّ} with both in the nominative, on the basis that «وعد» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "Yes, their resurrection is a promise binding on Allah", and «حَقٌّ» is a naʿt of «وعدٌ».

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لِيُبَيِّنَ}: this lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb implied after the particle of affirmation, i.e. "Yes, He will resurrect them in order to make clear".

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كُنْ فَيَكُونُ}: that has already been given in al-Baqara. The lām in «لِشيءٍ» and in «له» is the lām of conveying (lām al-tablīgh), as in "I said to him: stand". Al-Zajjāj made it causal in both, i.e. "for the sake of a thing, that We say for its sake", and this is not clear. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "His saying, the Exalted, {أَن نَّقُولَ} is treated as a maṣdar (verbal noun), as though He said: 'Our saying'; but «أنْ» with the verb gives a future sense not found in the maṣdar in most of its uses, though it sometimes comes in places where time is not considered, like this verse and like His saying {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَن تَقُومَ السمآء والأرض بِأَمْرِهِ} [al-Rūm: 25], and other cases."
The Shaykh said: "His saying 'in most of its uses' is not good; rather it denotes the future in all its uses. And as for his saying 'though it sometimes comes …' to the end: that was not understood from «أنْ»; it was understood only from ascribing the standing of the heavens and the earth to Allah's command, because that is not restricted to the future rather than the past with respect to Him, the Exalted. Its parallel is {وَكَانَ الله غَفُوراً رَّحِيماً}: «كان» denotes the association of the content of the clause with past time, while He, the Exalted, / is characterised by that at every time."

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {حَسَنَةً}: there are several views on it. The first: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a good settling". The second: it is accusative as a maṣdar that coincides with its governor in meaning, because the meaning of «لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم» is "We shall surely do good to them". The third: it is a second object, because the verb before it carries the meaning of "We shall surely give them"; and «حسنة» is a naʿt of an omitted noun it qualifies, i.e. "a good abode" — in the exegesis of al-Ḥasan: a good abode, namely Medina. It was said: its implied form is "a good standing", namely victory over the people of the East and the West. It was said: «حسنة» itself is the object, without the omission of a qualified noun.
The Commander of the Believers [ʿAlī], Ibn Masʿūd and Nuʿaym ibn Maysara read «لَنُثْوِيَنَّهُمْ» with thāʾ (three dots) and yāʾ, the imperfect of athwā, transferred by the transitivising hamza from thawā, meaning "to reside"; it will come that it was read so among the Seven in al-ʿAnkabūt. «حسنةً» is as already described, and we add that it may be accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "in a good [abode]".
The relative noun is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause made up of the omitted oath and its answer is its khabar (predicate); in this there is a refutation of Thaʿlab, who disallowed an oath clause being a khabar. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «الذين» to be accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb) with an implied verb, i.e. "We shall surely settle those who …". The Shaykh rejected this on the ground that only what may govern can explain [an implied] governor; and if you said "Zaydan la-aḍribanna" it would not be permissible, so likewise "Zaydan la-aḍribannahu" is not permissible.
His saying: {لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: the pronoun may refer back to the disbelievers, i.e. had they known that, they would have returned as Muslims; or to the believers, i.e. they would have striven in emigration and good deeds as others did.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying, the Exalted: {الذين صَبَرُواْ}: its position is nominative on [the implied] «هم», or accusative on [the implied] «أمدحُ» ("I praise"); and it may follow the relative noun before it as a naʿt (adjective), badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), so its position is that one's position.

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying, the Exalted: {نوحي إِلَيْهِمْ}: it has already been given at the end of Yūsuf. A group read «يُوحي», i.e. Allah.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بالبينات}: there are eight views on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word] on the basis that it is a naʿt (adjective) of «رِجالاً», so it is attached to an omitted [word], i.e. "men clothed with the clear proofs", i.e. accompanied by them. This is a good view, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī, with nothing objectionable in it. The second: it is attached to «أَرْسَلْنا», mentioned by al-Ḥawfī, al-Zamakhsharī and others, and al-Zamakhsharī began with it. He said: "It is attached to «أَرسَلْنا», coming under the rule of the exception together with «رجالاً», i.e. 'We sent only men with the clear proofs', as when you say: 'I struck only Zayd with the whip', because its origin is: 'I struck Zayd with the whip'." Abū al-Baqāʾ declared it weak on the ground that what precedes «إلاَّ» does not govern what follows it [Translator's note: printed «بعدهم», evidently for «بعدها»] when the sentence is complete with «إلا» and what follows it. He said: "Except that it has occurred in poetry:
297 - 1- نُبِّئْتُهُمْ عَذَّبوا بالنارِ جارتَهمْ ... ولا يُعَذِّبَ إلا الله بالنارِ
(I was told that they tormented their female neighbour with fire — and none torments with fire but Allah.)"
The Shaykh said: "What al-Ḥawfī and al-Zamakhsharī allowed, the Basrans do not allow, since they do not allow anything to come after «إلا» except the excepted, or that from which the exception is made, or what follows these; and whatever appears otherwise has a governor estimated for it.
