Al-Kisāʾī allowed what is governed by what precedes it to follow it, whether nominative, accusative or genitive, as in: 'none struck but ʿAmran — Zayd', 'none struck but Zaydun — ʿAmran', and 'none passed but Zaydun by ʿAmr'. Ibn al-Anbārī agreed with him on the nominative, and al-Akhfash on the adverb and its equivalent; so what they met with works on the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash." [Translator's note: the name is printed «الزمشخريُّ» in the source, evidently for al-Zamakhsharī.]
The third: it is also attached to «أَرْسَلْنا», except that it is intended to be placed before the particle of exception, its implied form being: "We did not send before you with the clear proofs and the scriptures except men", so that what follows «إلا» are not two governed elements, delayed in wording and in rank, coming under the restriction, of what precedes «إلا»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported it.
The fourth: it is attached to «نُوحِي», as you say "it was revealed to him with truth"; mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ. The fifth: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in «بالبيِّنات», and on this view «بالبيِّنات» is what stands in place of the agent, because they are what is revealed. The sixth: the preposition with its noun is attached to an omitted [word] on the basis that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what stands in place of the agent, namely «إليهم». Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned both, and both are very weak in meaning and in grammatical craft.
The seventh: it is attached to «لا تعلمون», on the basis that the condition / is in the sense of rebuke and binding argument, as when a hired worker says: "If I have worked for you, then give me my due." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And His saying «فاسْألوا أهلَ» is parenthetical on the preceding views"; by His saying «فاسألوا» he means the apodosis and its protasis. As for the last view, the absence of parenthesis is clear.
The eighth: it is attached to an omitted [verb] as the answer to an implied question, as though it were said: "With what were they sent?" and it was said: "They were sent with the clear proofs and the scriptures." So al-Zamakhsharī estimated it, and it is better than Abū al-Baqāʾ's estimation "they were dispatched", because it agrees in wording and meaning with what indicates it.

semin-durr:45-45.t: His saying, the Exalted: {السيئات}: there are three views on it. The first: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "the evil plots", and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «مَكَروا» being made to carry the sense of "they did, they performed"; on these two views His saying {أَن يَخْسِفَ الله} is the object of «أَمِنَ». The third: it is accusative by «أَمِنَ», i.e. "they felt secure from the evil punishments"; on this view His saying {أَن يَخْسِفَ الله} is a badal (substitute) from «السيئات».

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {على تَخَوُّفٍ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], for it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) either from the agent of «يأخذهم» or from its object; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned both.
The apparent view is that it is a ḥāl from the object, not the agent.
Al-takhawwuf: gradual diminishing (al-tanaqquṣ). Al-Zamakhsharī reported that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb asked them about it from the pulpit and they were silent; then an old man of Hudhayl stood and said: "This is our dialect: al-takhawwuf is gradual diminishing." He said: "Do [the Arabs] know that in their poetry?" He said: "Yes. Our poet said", and he recited:
297 - 2- تَخَوَّف الرَّحْلُ منها تامِكاً قَرِداً ... كما تَخَوَّفَ النَّبْعَةِ السَّفَنُ
(The saddle wore down from her a high, compact hump, as the rasp wears down [the wood of] the nabʿa tree.) [Translator's note: the verse is usually cited «كما تخوَّفَ عودَ النبعةِ السَّفَنُ»; reproduced as written in the source.]
ʿUmar said: "O people, hold fast to your register (dīwān), and you will not go astray." They said: "And what is our register?" He said: "The poetry of the Jāhiliyya, for in it is the explanation of your Book."
I say: al-Zamakhsharī had earlier attributed the verse to Zuhayr, and it seems to be an oversight, for it is by Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī; this is supported by the man's saying "our poet said", and he was a Hudhalī, as he himself reported. It was said: al-takhawwuf is fear (al-khawf).

semin-durr:90-90.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَإِيتَآءِ ذِي القربى}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object. He did not mention what العدل (justice), الإحسان (doing good) and البَغْي (transgression) relate to, so as to include everything in which justice is done, good is done to, and transgression is committed. For that reason He did not mention the second object of الإيتاء (giving), and He specified the first in order to urge it, because of the kinsman's claim through kinship, for giving to him is both charity and the maintaining of ties.
His words: «يَعِظُكم» may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), having the force of giving the reason for the command with what preceded, i.e. exhortation is the cause of His commanding you with that. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «يَنْهَى». His restricting the ḥāl to this governor alone is open to question, since it is apparent that it can be made a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «يأمرُ» as well — indeed that is more fitting, for exhortation is by commands and prohibitions, so it has no special connection with prohibition.

semin-durr:91-91.t:
The words of the Exalted: {بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb of prohibition. And التوكيد is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of وَكَّدَ يُوَكِّدُ with wāw; there is another dialectal form of it: أَكَّد يُؤَكِّد with hamza. This is like their saying وَرَّخْتُ الكتابَ and أرَّخْتُه (I dated the document). The hamza is not a substitute for a wāw, as Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] claimed, because the two usages in the two roots are equal, so claiming that one of them is original is no more fitting than the other.
Makkī followed al-Zajjāj in that, then said: "It is not good to say: the wāw is a substitute for the hamza, just as it is not good to say that in «أَحَد», since its origin is «وَحَد», so the hamza is a substitute for the wāw." He means that no one holds the reverse. Al-Zamakhsharī likewise followed him in that. And «تَوْكِيدها» is a maṣdar annexed to its object.
Abū ʿAmr assimilated the dāl into the tāʾ, and it has no second instance in the Qur'an — I mean that no dāl with fatḥa after a quiescent letter was assimilated except in this word.
His words: {وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ}: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either of the fāʿil (agent) of «تَنْقُضوا», or of the agent of the maṣdar, even though it is omitted.

semin-durr:92-92.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَنكَاثاً}: two views are possible in it. The more apparent: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «غَزْلها» (her yarn). And الأَنْكاث is the plural of نِكْث in the sense of مَنْكوث, i.e. undone. The second: it is a second object, because «نَقَضَتْ» is made to include the meaning of «صَيَّرَتْ» (she made it into). Al-Zajjāj allowed a third view in it, namely the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of نَقَضَتْ is نَكَثَتْ, so it coincides with its governor in meaning.
His words: «تَتَّخذون»: the clause may be a ḥāl of the wāw of «تكونوا», or of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the prepositional phrase, since the meaning is: do not be resembling such-and-such while you are taking.
His words: {دَخَلاً بَيْنَكُمْ}: it is the second object of «تَتَّخذون». And الدَّخَل is corruption and deceit. It is said: «دَخَلاً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). And it is said: الدَّخَل is what enters into a thing while not being of it.
His words: {أَن تَكُونَ}, i.e. because of [one community] being, or for fear of [one community] being. «تكون» may be complete (tāmma), so that «أمَّةٌ» is its fāʿil (agent); or it may be incomplete (nāqiṣa), so that «أمَّةٌ» is its noun (ism), «هي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أَرْبَى» its khabar (predicate). The clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl on the first view, and in the position of the khabar on the second. The Kufans [Translator's note: the source has «الموفيون», evidently a misprint for «الكوفيون», the Kufans] allowed «أُمَّةٌ» to be its noun, with «هي» as a ʿimād (support), i.e. a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and «أربَى» the khabar of «تكون». The Basrans do not allow that because the noun is indefinite; if the noun were definite, that would be permissible according to them.
His words: «به»: the pronoun may refer back to the maṣdar formed from {أَن تَكُونَ}, its implied form being: "Allah only tests you by the being of a community", i.e. He tries you with that. It is said: it refers back to «الربا» (the surpassing) indicated by His words {هِيَ أَرْبَى}. And it is said: to the abundance, because it is in the sense of "the many". Ibn al-Anbārī said: "Since its feminine is not real, it was treated according to the sense of the masculine, just as الصيحة (the shout) was treated as الصِّياح." Yet no word for "abundance" has preceded; it is only indicated by the meaning from His words {هِيَ أَرْبَى}.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَتَزِلَّ}: in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ», in answer to the prohibition.
His words: {بِمَا صَدَدتُّمْ}: «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and «صَدَدْتُمْ» may be from الصُّدود (turning away oneself), or from الصَدّ (turning others away), its object being omitted. And «قَدَمٌ» was made indefinite. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was the foot made singular and indefinite? I say: to make it a grave matter that a single foot should slip from the path of truth after having stood firm upon it — so how then about many feet?"
The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "In a plural, sometimes the aggregate as an aggregate is considered, and sometimes each single individual is considered. When the aggregate is considered in it, the predication takes account of plurality; and when each single individual is considered in it, the predication frequently agrees with the plural wording, so what is predicated of it is made plural; or agrees with each single individual, so it is made singular, as in the words of the Exalted: {وَأَعْتَدَتْ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَئاً وَآتَتْ}, since in His words «لهنَّ» the sense 'for each one of them' was considered; had it come intending plurality, or the frequent usage in the second view, المتكأ would have been made plural. On this sense the words of the poet are understood:
301 - 5- فإني وَجَدْتُ الضَّامِرينَ متاعُهمْ ... يَمُوْتُ ويَفْنَى فارْضِخِي مِنْ وعائيا
(For I have found that the lean ones — their provision dies and perishes; so give a little from my vessel.)
i.e. I have seen every lean one; that is why he made the pronoun singular in «يموتُ ويَفْنى». And since the meaning is: let not each one of you take, «فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمٌ» came in keeping with this meaning; then He said: «وتَذُوقُوا», in keeping with the aggregate, [or] with the plural wording in the frequent usage if we say that the predication is to each single individual. So the verse has addressed the prohibition of taking oaths as a means of deceit with regard to the aggregate and with regard to each single individual, and indicated that by the singular «قَدَم» and by the plural pronoun in «وتَذُوْقوا»."
I say: with this interpretation which the Shaykh mentioned, the weighty meaning which Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] captured from the indefiniteness and singularity of «قَدَم» is lost. As for the verse mentioned, the grammarians explained it as meaning: "there dies whoever is there, and whoever is mentioned", so he made the pronoun singular for that reason, not for what he mentioned.

semin-durr:96-96.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And النَّفَاد is perishing and passing away. One says: نَفِذ, with kasra on the ʿayn, يَنْفَذُ, with fatḥa on it, نَفَاذاً ونُفُوذاً. [Translator's note: the source writes these forms with dhāl («نَفِذ», «يَنْفَذُ», «نَفَاذاً», «نُفُوذاً»), whereas the context, which goes on to contrast the root with dhāl, requires dāl: نَفِد يَنْفَد نَفاداً; kept as printed.] As for «نَفَذَ» with the dotted dhāl, its verb is نَفَذَ with fatḥa, يَنْفُذُ with ḍamma; and it will come. One says: أَنْفَد القومُ: their provisions ran out. And خَصْمٌ مُنافِدٌ: an adversary who seeks to exhaust his opponent's argument; one says: نافَدْتُه فَنَفِدْتُه (I contended with him in exhausting arguments and outlasted him).
And His words «باقٍ»: the discussion of pausing on it has preceded in al-Raʿd.
His words: {وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ الذين}: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim and Ibn Dhakwān read {وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ} with the nūn of majesty, as an iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person to the first person; the explanation of iltifāt has preceded. The rest read it with the yāʾ of the third person, returning to Allah because His mighty name was mentioned before in the words of the Exalted: {وَمَا عِندَ الله بَاقٍ}.
And His words: {بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ}: the afʿal may have its usual sense of preference (tafḍīl); and if He rewards them with the best, then that He should reward them with the good follows a fortiori. It is also said: it is not for preference; it is as though they fled from the implication (mafhūm) of afʿal, since rewarding with the best does not entail rewarding with the good. That is a mistake, because of what preceded: that it belongs to the concordant implication (mafhūm al-muwāfaqa) by way of a fortiori.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مِّن ذَكَرٍ}: «مِنْ» is explicative (li-l-bayān), so it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "I mean: of male". And it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «عَمِل».
His words: {وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ}: also a circumstantial clause.
His words: {وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ}: He observed the meaning of «مَنْ» and so made the pronoun plural, after having observed its wording and so made it singular in «فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ» and what precedes it. The majority read «وَلَجْزِيَنَّهم» [Translator's note: so printed in the source; the Qur'anic wording is «وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهم»] with the nūn of majesty, in keeping with what precedes. Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission read it with the yāʾ of the third person; this ought to be on the basis of an implied second oath, so that it is a conjunction of an oath clause to an oath clause like it, both oaths being omitted and their answers remaining.
It is not possible for it to be a conjunction of an answer to an answer, because this would lead to the speaker reporting about himself with a third-person report, which is not permitted. If you said: «زيد قال: واللهِ لأَضْرِبَنَّ هنداً ولَينفينَّها», meaning "and Zayd will surely banish her", it would not be permitted. But if you implied another oath, it would be permitted, i.e. "and he said: by Allah, he will surely banish her"; because in such a construction you may relate his wording — and of this is {وَلَيَحْلِفُنَّ إِنْ أَرَدْنَا إِلاَّ الحسنى} [al-Tawba: 107] — or relate its meaning — and of this is {يَحْلِفُونَ بالله مَا قَالُواْ} [al-Tawba: 74]; had it come according to the wording, it would have been said: "we did not say".

semin-durr:98-98.t: The words of the Exalted: {فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ}: i.e. "when you intend [to recite]", so the intention is implied. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because the act comes into being upon the aim and the intention without any interval and in accordance with it, so it has a strong connection and an evident association with it." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«إذا» is a link between the two parts of speech, and the Arabs use it in the like of this; the implied form of the verse is: when you begin reciting the Qur'an, seek refuge." I say: this is the position of the majority of the readers and scholars. Some took the outward sense of the verse and sought refuge after reciting: of the Companions, Abū Hurayra; of the imams, Mālik and Ibn Sīrīn; and of the readers, Ḥamza.

semin-durr:100-100.t: The words of the Exalted: {بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ}: the pronoun may refer back to Satan, and this is the apparent view, so that the pronouns are uniform. The meaning is: and those who are associators because of him. It is also said: and those who, by their associating Iblīs, associate partners with Allah. And it may refer back to «ربهم».

semin-durr:101-101.t: The words of the Exalted: {والله أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُنَزِّلُ}: there are two views on this clause. The more apparent: it is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) between the condition and its apodosis. The second: it is circumstantial, and that is not apparent. And His words: {إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُفْتَرٍ}: they ascribed fabrication to him ﷺ with several kinds of intensification: restriction (al-ḥaṣr), direct address, and the active participle, which indicates permanence and stability. The object of «لا يَعْلمون» is omitted because it is known, i.e. they do not know that in the abrogation of laws and of some of the Qur'an there are far-reaching wisdoms.

semin-durr:102-102.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِيُثَبِّتَ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «نَزَّله». And «هدى وبشرى» may be conjoined to the position of «ليُثَبِّتَ», and so be in the accusative; or to its wording, with regard to the interpreted maṣdar, and so be in the genitive. The words of al-Zamakhsharī on their like have preceded, together with what the Shaykh rebutted him with and what was rebutted against the Shaykh. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed them to be nominative as two predicates of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and it is guidance", the clause being a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And it was read «لِيُثْبِتَ», without doubling, from أَثْبتَ.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِّسَانُ الذي}: the majority read «لسان» annexed to what follows it. And اللِّسان is language. Al-Ḥasan read «اللسان», made definite with al-, with «الذي» as a naʿt (adjective) of it. There are two views on this clause. The first: it has no position, being resumptive; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يقولون», i.e. they say that while the situation is this, i.e. their knowledge of the non-Arabness of this human and the clear Arabness of this Qur'an ought to have prevented them from that saying; as when you say: "You revile so-and-so while he has done good to you", i.e. your knowledge of his doing good to you ought to have prevented you from reviling him. The Shaykh said this. Then he said: "He [al-Zamakhsharī] took the view of resumption and not of the ḥāl only because it is part of his doctrine that a nominal ḥāl clause without wāw is anomalous; and that is a weaker position in which he followed al-Farrāʾ."
And «أعجميٌّ» is the khabar (predicate) on both readings. And الأعجميّ is one who does not speak Arabic. Al-Rāghib said: "العَجَم are the opposite of the Arabs, and العجميّ is one attributed to them. And الأَعْجَم is one in whose tongue there is an impediment (ʿujma), whether Arab or non-Arab, with regard to the paucity of understanding [others have] of him because of the impediment. And الأعجميّ is attributed to it; from this the beast was called «عَجْماءُ», inasmuch as it does not express itself clearly, and "the prayer of the daytime is ʿajmāʾ", i.e. it is not recited aloud. And العَجَم: date-stones, because they are hidden. As for حروف المعجم (the letters of the alphabet), al-Khalīl said: 'the disjointed letters, because they are aʿjamiyya'. Some said: its meaning is that the bare letters do not indicate what joined letters indicate. And أَعْجمتُ الكتاب is the opposite of أَعْرَبْتُه; and أَعْجَمْتُه: I removed its obscurity, like أَشْكَيْتُه, i.e. I removed his complaint." Further explanation of this will come too, Allah willing, in al-Shuʿarāʾ and Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda. The readers' disagreement over «يُلْحِدُون» has preceded in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَوَ لَمَْ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «تَرَوْا» in the second person, in keeping with His saying {فَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ}, and the rest with yāʾ, in keeping with His saying {أَفَأَمِنَ الذين مَكَرُواْ}. As for His saying {أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إلى الطير} [al-Naḥl: 79], Ḥamza also read it in the second person, and Ibn ʿĀmir agreed with him in it. So from the two verses together it results that Ḥamza has the second person in both; al-Kisāʾī the second person in the first and the third person in the second; Ibn ʿĀmir the reverse; and the rest the third person in both.
As for the justification of the first, it has already been given. As for the second person in the second, it is in keeping with His saying {والله أَخْرَجَكُم مِّن بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ} [al-Naḥl: 78]; and the third person is in keeping with His saying {وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ الله} [al-Naḥl: 73]. As for al-Kisāʾī's and Ibn ʿĀmir's distinguishing between the two places, it is to combine the two considerations, and [to show] that each of them is sound.
His saying: {مِن شَيْءٍ}: this is an explanation of «ما» in His saying {مَا خَلَقَ الله}, for it is a relative noun in the sense of «الذي». If you say: how can the relative noun — which is vague — be explained by «شيء», which is vague, indeed vaguer than what precedes it? The answer is that «شيء» has become clear and evident through being described by the clause after it, namely {يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ}.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ما» is a relative noun with {خَلَقَ الله} [as its ṣila], and it is vague; its explanation is {مِن شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ}." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "His saying {مِن شَيْءٍ} is a general expression covering everything that the description in His saying {يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ} entails." The apparent sense of these two statements is that the clause {يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ} is a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء». As for someone else, he stated explicitly that the clause is not a naʿt, for he said: "The meaning is: of anything that has a shadow, such as a mountain, a tree, a building or a standing body. His saying {يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ} is a statement about His saying {مِن شَيْءٍ}, not a description of it, and this statement indicates that omitted description whose implied form is: it has a shadow." This involves a strain for which there is no need, and the naʿt is clearer. {مِن شَيْءٍ} is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, or attached to an omitted [verb] by way of explanation, i.e. "I mean: of anything".
Al-tafayyuʾ is tafaʿʿala from fāʾa, yafīʾu, i.e. "to return". «فاء» is intransitive; when it is meant to be transitive it is made transitive by the hamza, as in His saying, the Exalted: {مَّآ أَفَآءَ / الله على رَسُولِهِ} [al-Ḥashr: 7], or by doubling, as in: fayyaʾa Allāhu al-ẓilla fa-tafayyaʾa (Allah made the shade turn, so it turned). Tafayyaʾa is a reflexive-resultative (muṭāwiʿ) form, so it is intransitive. It occurs as transitive in the poetry of Abū Tammām, in his saying:
297 - 3- طَلَبَتْ ربيعَ ربيعةَ المُمْرَى لها ... وتفيَّأَتْ ظلالَه مَمْدودا
(She sought the spring-pasture of Rabīʿa, made to yield for her, and sheltered in its shade (tafayyaʾat ẓilālahu), extended.)
There is disagreement about al-fayʾ. It was said: it is shade in general, whether before or after the decline of the sun from the meridian (al-zawāl), and this agrees with the meaning of the verse here. It was said: "What is [before] the zawāl is ẓill only, and what is after it is both ẓill and fayʾ", so ẓill is more general; this is narrated from Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj. It was said: rather ẓill is specific to what is before the zawāl and fayʾ to what is after it. Al-Azharī said: "The tafayyuʾ of shadows is their returning after midday; so tafayyuʾ is only in the evening and [in] what the sun has turned away from, and ẓill is what is in the morning, which is what [the sun] has not reached." The poet said:
297 - 5- فلا الظِلُّ مِنْ بَرْدِ الضُّحى تَسْتطيعُه ... ولا الفيْءُ من بَرْدِ العَشِيِّ تَذُوْقُ
(You can neither reach the shade (ẓill) in the cool of the forenoon, nor taste the fayʾ in the cool of the evening.) [Translator's note: this verse and the next are both numbered «297 - 5» in the source; reproduced as written.]
Imruʾ al-Qays also said:
297 - 5- تَيَمَّمَتِ العينَ التي عند ضارِجٍ ... يَفِيْءُ عليها الظِّلُّ عَرْمَضُها طامِ
(She made for the spring at Ḍārij, over which the shade turns (yafīʾu), its green scum overflowing.)
Ibn Qutayba faulted people for applying fayʾ to what is before the zawāl, and said it is applied only to what is after it; he argued from the derivation, for fayʾ is returning, and that is realised only after the zawāl, since the shadow returns toward the east after the zawāl, after the sun had effaced it before the zawāl.
Abū ʿAmr read «تَتَفَيَّأ» with tāʾ (dots above), in regard to the feminine of the plural, and Yaʿqūb read it so; the rest read with yāʾ because the feminine is figurative.
The majority read «ظلالُه», plural of ẓill, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar «ظُلَلُهُ», plural of «ظُلَّة», like ghurfa / ghuraf. The author of al-Lawāmiḥ said on ʿĪsā's reading «ظُلَلُهُ»: "Al-ẓulla is cloud, which is a body; and with kasra it is the fayʾ, which is an accident. ʿĪsā considered that tafayyuʾ, which is returning, is more fitting for bodies than for accidents; in the reading of the majority it is by way of metaphor."
His saying: «عن اليمين»: there are three views on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يتفيَّأ», and its meaning is passing beyond, i.e. the shadows pass from the right to the left. The second: it is attached to an omitted [word] on the basis that it is a ḥāl from «ظلالُه». The third: it [«عن»] is a noun meaning "side", and on this view it is accusative as an adverb.
His saying: {عَنِ اليمين والشمآئل}: there are two questions about it. One: what is meant by the right and the lefts? The second: how did He make the first singular and the second plural [Translator's note: printed «وجوع», evidently for «وجمع»]? The first was answered with several answers. One: the right is the right of the celestial sphere, which is the east, and the lefts are its left, which is the west; these two sides were singled out because the strongest parts of a human being are his two sides, his right and his left; and He made the east the right because the daily motion of the sphere appears from it.
The second: in a town whose latitude is less than the declination of the sun, the sun in summer is to the right of the town, so the shadow falls to their right.
The third: what is set up as a lesson is every body that has a shadow, such as mountains and trees, while that for which right and left are arranged is only human beings; but the mention of right and left here is by way of metaphor.
The fourth: al-Zamakhsharī said: "Have they not seen what Allah has created of bodies that have shadows turning from their rights and their lefts — from the two sides of each one of them and its two flanks — by a metaphor from a person's right and left for the two sides of a thing, i.e. they return from one side to the other?" This is close to what precedes it.
The second was answered with several answers. One: the beginning takes place from the right, which is a single thing, so He made the right singular; then it diminishes little by little, state after state, / so it has the sense of plurality, and the word "left" applies to each state, so it became multiple with the multiplicity of the states. Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined to something close to this.
The second: al-Zamakhsharī said: "«اليمين» is in the sense of al-aymān (the rights)", meaning that it is a singular standing in place of the plural; so in meaning both are plurals, as in His saying {وَيُوَلُّونَ الدبر} [al-Qamar: 45], i.e. the backs.
The third: al-Farrāʾ said: "It is as though, when He used the singular, He had in mind one of the things that have shadows, and when He used the plural, He had in mind all of them, because His saying {مَا خَلَقَ الله مِن شَيْءٍ} is singular in wording and plural in meaning; so He expressed one of them with the singular wording, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَجَعَلَ الظلمات والنور} [al-Anʿām: 1] and His saying: {خَتَمَ الله على قُلُوبِهمْ وعلى سَمْعِهِمْ} [al-Baqara: 7]."
The fourth: if we explain the right as the east, then the point that is the rising-place of the sun is one particular point, so the right is one; as for the lefts, they are expressions for the deviations occurring in those shadows after they fall on the ground, and these are many, so He expressed them with the plural form.
The fifth: al-Kirmānī said: "It may be that by the lefts are meant the left, the back and the front, because the shadow turns from all the directions; so He began with the right because the turning begins from it, or seeking blessing by mentioning it; then He gathered the rest under the word 'left', because of the opposition between right and left, and treated the front and the back like the lefts, because of the difference between them and the right."
The sixth: Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What some people said — that the right is the first falling of the shadow after the zawāl, then the other, at sunset, is to the lefts, and that for this reason He made the lefts plural and the right singular — is a confusion of speech and is invalid in several respects. Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'When you have prayed the dawn prayer, what is between the rising-place of the sun and its setting-place is shade; then Allah sent the sun over it as a guide, and drew the shade in towards Him.' On this basis, at the first rising of the sun the shadow is to the right of one who faces south; then the deviation begins, and it is to the lefts, because it is many movements and broken shadows, so they are many lefts; and the shadow to the right was one continuous [shadow], covering everything."
The seventh: Ibn al-Ḍāʾiʿ said: "He used the singular and the plural with regard to the two extremes, because the morning shadow dwindles until only a little of it remains, so it is as though it were in one direction; and in the evening it is the reverse, because it spreads over all directions; so the two extremes were considered in the verse. This is from the side of meaning. As for the side of wording, there is correspondence in it, because «سُجَّداً» is plural, so the plural «الشمائل» corresponds to it, being adjacent to it. So there is in the verse a correspondence of wording to meaning and the consideration of both together, and that is the utmost of inimitability (iʿjāz)."
His saying: «سُجَّداً»: a ḥāl from «ظلالُه»; «سُجَّداً» is the plural of sājid, like shāhid / shuhhad and rākiʿ / rukkaʿ.
His saying: {وَهُمْ دَاخِرُونَ}: there are three views on this clause. The first: it is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «ظلالُه». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because it has the sense of the plural, namely whatever Allah created of anything that has a shadow; and it was made plural with wāw and nūn because humility (dukhūr) is among the attributes of rational beings, or because among all of that there are rational beings, so they were given precedence."
The Shaykh rejected this on the ground that the majority do not allow a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct); it is like "the servant of Hind came to me laughing (fem.)". He said: "Whoever allows it from that when the muḍāf is a part or like a part would allow it to be a ḥāl from it here, because the shadow is like a part, since it arises from it."
The second: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in «سُجَّدا», so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila).
The third: it is a ḥāl from «ظلالُه», so two ḥāls are accusative from it.
Then you have two ways of regarding this wāw. One: you make it conjoin one ḥāl to another like it, so it is a conjunction and not the wāw of ḥāl — even though a nominal clause serving as a ḥāl without the wāw is rare, or, on one opinion, impossible. Among those who stated explicitly that it is a conjunction is Abū al-Baqāʾ. The second: it is the wāw of ḥāl; on this view it may be asked: how can the governor require two ḥāls? The answer is that this is permissible because the second is a badal (substitute) from the first: if by prostration is meant self-abasement and submission, it is / a badal of the whole from the whole; and if its literal sense is meant, it is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), since prostration includes humility. The parallel of what we are dealing with is: "Zayd came laughing, while he was complaining": your saying "while he was complaining" may be a ḥāl from «زيد» or from the pronoun of «ضاحكاً».
Al-dukhūr: humility. He said:
297 - 6- فلم يَبْقَ إلا داخِرٌ في مُخَيَّسٍ ... ومُنْجَحِرٌ في غير أرضِكَ في جُحْرِ
(None remained but one humbled (dākhir) in a prison, and one hiding in a hole in a land not yours.)
It was said: it is subjugation and being overpowered. The meaning of «داخِرُون» is: abased and humbled.

semin-durr:106-106.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَن كَفَرَ بالله}: several views are possible in it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) of {الذين لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ}, i.e. only he who disbelieves fabricates lies. The second: it is a badal of «الكاذبون». The third: of «أولئك»; al-Zamakhsharī said this. On the first view, His words {وأولئك هُمُ الكاذبون} are a parenthetical clause between the badal and that for which it substitutes.
The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] considered the three views weak, saying: "Because the first entails that no one fabricates lies except one who disbelieves in Allah after his belief, whereas reality dictates that the fabricator is whoever does not believe, whether he disbelieved in Allah after his belief or not; indeed the majority is the second, and he is the fabricator." He said: "As for the second, the meaning comes back to that, since the implied form is: and those, i.e. those who do not believe, are the ones who disbelieved in Allah after their belief, and those who do not believe are the fabricators. And the third likewise, since the implied form is: those pointed to are the ones who disbelieved in Allah after their belief, it being stated of them that they are the liars."
The fourth view: it is in the accusative by way of censure (al-dhamm); al-Zamakhsharī said this. The fifth: it is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), also by way of censure. The sixth: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with an omitted khabar, its implied form being: "upon them is wrath", because what comes after the second «مَنْ» indicates it.
The seventh: it is also a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar — which is also the khabar of the second «مَنْ» — is His words {فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ}; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, and he said: "Since it is one in meaning, because by the statement in His words {مَن كَفَرَ بالله} only the category that opens [its breast] to disbelief is intended." The Shaykh said: "Even if this is as he mentioned, they are two conditional sentences, separated by the particle of rectification (istidrāk), so each of them on its own must have an apodosis which they do not share; so implying an omission is more in line with the craft of iʿrāb. They have considered weak the position of al-Akhfash in his claim that His words {فَسَلاَمٌ لَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ اليمين} [al-Wāqiʿa: 91] and His words {فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 89] are the answer to «أمَّا» and to this «إنْ», these being two conditional particles, one following the other."
The eighth: «مَنْ» is conditional and its apodosis is implied, its implied form being: "upon them is wrath", because what comes after the second «مَنْ» indicates it. It has preceded that Ibn ʿAṭiyya made the apodosis belong to both together, and the discussion with him about that has preceded.
His words: {إِلاَّ مَنْ أُكْرِهَ}: there are several views on it. The first: it is an excepted word placed in advance, from His words {فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِّنَ الله}; in this case it is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), because the one under compulsion did not open his breast to disbelief. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is said: it is not placed in advance, so it is like the words of Labīd:
301 - 6- ألا كلُّ شيءٍ ما خلا اللهَ باطلُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Lo, everything except Allah is vain …)"
The apparent sense of his words indicates that Labīd's verse has no advancement in it, and that is not so, for it is very evidently a case of advancement.
The second: it is excepted from the apodosis of the condition, or from the khabar of the implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "upon them is wrath from Allah, except one who is compelled"; that is why al-Zamakhsharī placed the implied apodosis of the condition before the exception. It is a joined (muttaṣil) exception, because disbelief may be by speech without conviction, as with the one compelled, and it may be — Allah forbid — with conviction; so He excepted the first category.
His words: {وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ}: a circumstantial clause, i.e. except one who is compelled in this state.
His words: {ولكن مَّن شَرَحَ}: the istidrāk (rectification) is clear, because with His words {إِلاَّ مَنْ أُكْرِهَ} the mind might jump to an unrestricted exception, so He rectified this. And His words {وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ} do not remove that misconception. And «مَنْ» is either conditional or relative; but whenever it is made conditional, a mubtadaʾ must be implied before it, because conditional sentences do not follow it [i.e. «لكن»] — the Shaykh said this, then said: "Its like is:
301 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولكن متى يَسْتَرْفِدِ القومُ أَرْفِدِ
(… but whenever the people seek help, I give help.)
i.e. but I, whenever they seek help." The conditional did not occur after «لكن» only because rectification does not occur in conditions — so it was said, and this is disputed.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ذلك بِأَنَّهُمُ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), like parallels that have passed. The reference of «ذلك» is to the wrath and punishment that were mentioned; that is why it is singular, as in His words {بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68] and [his words]:
301 - 8- كأنه في الجِلْدِ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
(As though it were, in the skin …)
and that has passed.

semin-durr:110-110.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ}: there are three views on the khabar (predicate) of this «إنَّ». [The first:] it is His words {لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ}, and the second {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ} with its noun is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first with its noun, as though it were said: "then indeed your Lord, indeed your Lord is Forgiving, Merciful". In that case two views are possible in His words «للذين»: that it is attached to the two predicates by way of tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one word), or to something omitted by way of clarification (bayān), as though it were said: "the forgiveness and the mercy are for those who emigrated". The second: the khabar is the prepositional phrase itself after it, as you say: إنَّ زيداً لك (Zayd is for you), i.e. he is for you, not against you, meaning He is their helper, not their forsaker. Al-Zamakhsharī said the substance of this [then said: "as the king is for a man, not against him, so he is protected and benefited"].
The third: the khabar of the first is dispensed with by the khabar of the second, meaning that it is omitted in wording because what follows indicates it. This is the meaning of Abū al-Baqāʾ's words: "It is said: the first «إنَّ» has no khabar in wording, because the khabar of the second suffices for it." In that case the Shaykh's rebuttal of him is not good, when he said: "This is not good, in that he cancelled the ruling of the first and gave the ruling to the second, which is the reverse of what preceded, and it is not permitted."
His words: {مِن بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُواْ}: Ibn ʿĀmir read «فَتَنوا» in the active voice, i.e. they put themselves to trial. If the pronoun refers back to the believers, the meaning is: they put themselves to trial by what they outwardly gave the polytheists in speech; or that, since they endured the torment of the polytheists, it is as though they put themselves to trial. And if it refers back to the polytheists, it is clear, i.e. they persecuted the believers.
The rest read «فُتِنُوا» in the passive. And the pronoun in «بعدها» is for the maṣdars understood from the preceding verbs, i.e. after the trial, the emigration, the striving and the patience. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It refers back to the trial, or the deed, or the emigration, or the repentance."

semin-durr:111-111.t:
The words of the Exalted: {يَوْمَ تَأْتِي}: it may be in the accusative by «رحيم»; that does not entail restricting His mercy to the adverb of time, because if He shows mercy on this day, then His mercy on other days is all the more fitting and apt. Or it may be in the accusative by an implied «اذكر» (remember). He observed the meaning of «كل» and so made the pronouns feminine in His words «تجادل» to the end; and its like is:
301 - 9- جادَتْ عليه كلُّ عَيْنٍ ثَرَّةٍ ... فتركْنَ كلَّ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Every abundant cloud-spring poured upon it, and they left every …)
except that in the verse he added the plural according to the meaning; and that has preceded at the beginning of this topic. And His words {وَهُمْ لاَ يُظْلَمُونَ}: He construed according to the meaning, and therefore made it plural.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
The words of the Exalted: {والخوف}: the majority read «الخوف» in the genitive, conjoined to «الرجوع» [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is «الجوع» (hunger)]. Its accusative is related from Abū ʿAmr, and there are several views on it. The first: it is conjoined to «لباس». The second: it is conjoined to the position of «الجوع», because it is in meaning the object of the maṣdar, the implied form being: "that He clothed them with hunger and fear"; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and it is far-fetched, because اللباس is the name for what is worn, and it is an eloquent metaphor, as I will point out to you. The third: it is in the accusative by an implied verb; Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī said this. [The fourth: it involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.] "and the garment of fear", then it was omitted and [the muḍāf ilayhi] was put in its place; al-Zamakhsharī said this.
The aspect of the metaphor is what al-Zamakhsharī said, for he said: "If you say: the tasting and the garment are two metaphors, so what makes them sound? And the metaphorical tasting is made to fall upon the metaphorical garment, so what makes its falling upon it sound? I say: tasting has come to function among them as a literal expression because of its frequency regarding afflictions and hardships and what touches people of them; so they say: so-and-so tasted misery and harm, and the tasting of punishment. What is perceived of the effect of harm and pain was likened to what is perceived of the taste of the bitter and the repugnant. As for the garment, what covers a person and clings to him of certain events was likened to it because of its enveloping the wearer. As for making the tasting fall upon the garment of hunger and fear, it is because, since it came as an expression for what covers and clings of them, it is as though it were said: so He made them taste what covered them of hunger and fear. They have two ways in this. The first: that they look in it to the thing for which the metaphor is borrowed (al-mustaʿār lahu), as He looked to it here; and like it are the words of Kuthayyir:
302 - 0- غَمْرُ الرِّداءِ إذا تَبَسَّم ضاحكاً ... غَلِقَتْ لضَحْكَتِهِ رِقابُ المالِ
(Ample of mantle: when he smiles laughing, the necks of wealth become forfeit at his laughter.)
He borrowed the mantle for generosity, because it protects the honour of its owner as the mantle protects [Translator's note: the source has «صَوْتَ», evidently a misprint for «صَوْنَ», 'protecting'] what it is thrown over, and he described it as ample (ghamr), which is a description of generosity and bounty, not of a mantle, looking to the thing for which the metaphor is borrowed. The second: that they look in it to the borrowed thing (al-mustaʿār), as in his words:
302 - 1- يُنازعني رِدائي عَبْدُ عَمْرٍو ... رُوَيْدَك يا أخا عمرِو بن بكر
ليَ الشَّطْرُ الذي ملكَتْ يميني ... ودونَك فاعْتَجِر منه بِشَطْرِ
(ʿAbd ʿAmr contends with me for my mantle — gently, O brother of ʿAmr ibn Bakr! Mine is the half my right hand possesses; and here you are — wrap your head with a half of it.)
By his mantle he meant his sword; then he said: 'wrap your head with a half of it', so he looked to the borrowed thing in the word الاعتجار (wrapping the head). Had He looked to it in what we are dealing with, He would have said: 'so He clothed them with the garment of hunger and fear'; and Kuthayyir would have said: 'with a flowing mantle when he smiles'." End of quote. And this is the utmost that can be said about the metaphor.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Since that touched them directly, it became like a garment; and this is like the words of al-Aʿshā:
302 - 2- إذا ما الضَّجِيْعُ ثنى جِيْدَها ... تَثَنَّتْ عليه فكانَتْ لباسا
(When her bedfellow bends her neck, she bends over him and becomes a garment.)
And its like are the words of the Exalted: {هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَّكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَّهُنَّ} [al-Baqara: 187]; and its like are the words of the poet:
302 - 2- وقد لَبِسَتْ بعد الزبيرِ مُجاشِعٌ ... لباسَ التي حاضَتْ ولن تَغْسِل الدَّما
(After al-Zubayr, Mujāshiʿ have put on the garment of a woman who menstruated and will never wash away the blood.)
It is as though, since the disgrace touched them and clung to them, they had put it on."
And His words «فأذاقهم» are parallel to the words of the Exalted: {ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ العزيز الكريم} [al-Dukhān: 49], and parallel to the words of the poet:
302 - 3- دونَكَ ما جَنَيْتَه فاحْسُ وذُقْ ...
(Here is what you have reaped — so sip and taste.)
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «فأذاقها اللهُ الخوفَ والجوعَ», and in the codex of Ubayy: «لباسَ الخوفِ والجوعِ».
And His words {بِأَنْعُمِ الله}: He brought the plural of paucity and did not say «بِنِعَمِ الله», the plural of abundance, to point by the lesser to the greater; because if the punishment is for ingratitude for the little thing, then its being for the many blessings is all the more fitting.
And regarding «أنْعُم» there are two views. The first: it is the plural of «نِعْمة», like شِدَّة: أَشُدّ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The plural of «نِعمة», disregarding the tāʾ, like دِرْع and أَدْرُع." Quṭrub said: "It is the plural of نُعْم, and النُّعْم is comfort; one says: these are days of food and comfort (طُعْم ونُعْم)." And in the hadith: "The herald of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called out during the season at Minā: 'These are days of eating and enjoyment, so do not fast.'"
His words: {بِمَا كَانُواْ}: [«ما»] may be maṣdariyya (infinitival) or in the sense of "that which", the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. because of their doing, or because of what they used to do. The wāw in «يَصْنعون» refers back to the people of the punished one. It is said: a town, and it is parallel to His words {أَوْ هُمْ قَآئِلُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 4] after His words {وَكَم مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا}. [Translator's note: the source wording here, «أهل المعذَّب. قيل: قرية», appears garbled; the sense is that the pronoun refers to the people of the punished town (al-qarya), the town itself being mentioned in the singular.]

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن دَآبَّةٍ}: it may be an explanation of what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, in which case Allah the Exalted has in His heavens creatures that move about (yadibbūn) just as the creatures on earth move about. It may be an explanation of what is in the earth only. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was «مَنْ» not used instead of «ما», giving precedence to the rational among the creatures over the others? I say: because had «مَنْ» been used, there would have been no indication of giving precedence in it, and it would have been [Translator's note: printed «فكأن», evidently for «فكان»] covering the rational exclusively; so what is suitable for the rational and others was used, intending generality."
The Shaykh said: "The apparent sense of the question is the concession that «مَنْ» may include the rational and others by way of giving precedence, while the apparent sense of the answer is the restriction of «مَنْ» to the rational, and that what is suitable for the rational [and others] is «ما» and not «مَنْ». This is not an answer, because he raised the question on the basis of the concession and then gave the answer on a basis other than the concession; so the meaning became: «مَنْ» is used to give precedence, and the answer: it is not used to give precedence. In reality this is not an answer."
His saying: {وَهُمْ لاَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ}: the clause may be resumptive, informing about them with that, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَسْجُدُ».

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَخَافُونَ}: it may be explaining their not being arrogant, as though it were said: "Why are they not arrogant?" and that was given as the answer; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «لا يَسْتكبرون». The meaning of {يَخَافُونَ رَبَّهُمْ} is: [they fear] His punishment.
His saying: {مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ}: two views are possible on it. One: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَخافون», i.e. they fear the punishment of their Lord coming from above them, because punishment only comes down from above. The second: it is attached to an omitted [word] on the basis that it is a ḥāl from «ربهم», i.e. they fear their Lord as exalted above them, subduing them, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُوَ القاهر فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ} [al-Anʿām: 18].

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {اثنين}: there are two views on it. One: it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of «إلهَيْن», and most people hold this; on this view «اتَّخذ» may be transitive to one object, or transitive to two, the second of them being omitted, i.e. "do not take two gods as an object of worship".
The second: «اثنين» is the first object, only placed later, the origin being "do not take two as gods"; and this is far-fetched.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a second object", and this is something like an error, since there is no meaning to that at all. Al-Zamakhsharī's words here imply that it is not emphasis, for he said: "If you say: they combined the number and the thing counted only beyond one and two, saying 'I have men, three, and horses, four', because the thing counted is devoid of the specific number; as for rajul (a man) and rajulān (two men), faras (a horse) and farasān (two horses), they are counted nouns containing an indication of the number, so there is no need to say 'one man' and 'two men, two'. So what is the reason for His saying, the Exalted, {إلهين اثنين}? I say: the noun bearing the meaning of singular or dual denotes two things: the genus and the specific number. When it is intended to indicate that what is meant of the two, and what the discourse is driving at, is the number, it is paired with what emphasises the number, thereby indicating the intention toward it and the concern with it. Do you not see that if you said 'god' and did not emphasise it with 'one', it would not be good, and it would be imagined that you are affirming divinity, not oneness?"
The Shaykh said: "Since the noun coined for the singular and the dual may be used figuratively, meaning by it the genus, as in 'an excellent man is Zayd' and 'excellent men (dual) are the two Zayds', and the poet's saying: /
297 - 7- فإنَّ النارَ بالعُوْدَيْنِ تُذْكَى ... وإنَّ الحربَ أَوَّلُها الكلامُ
(For fire is kindled by two sticks, and war begins with words.)
— the noun coined for them was emphasised with the description, so it was said 'two gods, two', and it was said 'one god'."
His saying: «فإيَّايَ»: accusative by an implied verb estimated after it [Translator's note: printed «بعدهن», evidently for «بعده»], which this overt one explains, i.e. "Me fear, so fear Me". Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated it as "fear Me (irhabū iyyāya), so fear Me". The Shaykh said: "That is an oversight of the grammatical rule, which is that when the object is a detached pronoun and the verb is transitive to one object, the verb must be placed after it, as in {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ} [al-Fātiḥa: 5]; and it may not come first except by poetic licence, as in his saying:
297 - 8- إليك حتى بَلَغَتْ إيَّاكا ...
(… to you, until she reached you (iyyāka).)"
This has already been set out at the beginning of al-Baqara. Ibn ʿAṭiyya may be defended on the ground that what is ugly in matters of wording is not ugly in matters of estimation. In His saying «فإيَّايَ» there is iltifāt (a shift of person) from the third person, namely His saying {وَقَالَ الله}, to the first person, namely His saying «فإيَّاي»; then He shifted to the third person again in His saying: {وَلَهُ مَا فِي السماوات}.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَاصِباً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الدِّين», governed by the [notion of] being-established contained in the prepositional phrase that serves as the khabar (predicate). Al-wāṣib: lasting. Ḥassān said:
297 - 9- غَيَّرَتْهُ الريحُ تَسْفِي بِهِ ... وهَزِيْمٌ رَعْدُهُ واصِبُ
(The wind altered it, blowing dust over it, and a rumbling [cloud] whose thunder is constant (wāṣib).)
[And] Abū al-Aswad [said]:
298 - 0- لا أبتغيْ الحَمْدَ القليلَ بقاؤُه ... يوماً بِذَمِّ الدهرِ أَجْمَعَ واصِبا
(I do not seek praise of little endurance for a day at the price of blame lasting (wāṣib) all time.)
Al-waṣib: the sick, because illness persists with him. It was said: it is from al-waṣab, which is fatigue, and in that case it is by way of relation (nasab), i.e. "possessing fatigue", because religion contains duties and hardships for the servants; so it is like his saying:
298 - 1-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . أضحى فؤادي به فاتِنا
(… my heart became, through it, fātin [i.e. possessed of infatuation].)
i.e. possessing infatuation. It was said: al-wāṣib is the pure.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The wāw in His saying {وَلَهُ مَا فِي السماوات} conjoins to His saying {إله وَاحِدٌ}, and it may be a wāw of beginning (wāw al-ibtidāʾ)." The Shaykh said: "'Wāw of beginning' is said only of the wāw of ḥāl, and a ḥāl is not apparent here." I say: they sometimes say "wāw of beginning" meaning the resumptive wāw, i.e. the one with which neither conjunction nor association is intended; they have stated that explicitly, saying: the wāw may be brought at the beginning of speech without intending conjunction, and they cited as evidence their using it at the beginning of their odes and poems, which is very frequent. The meaning of his saying "conjoins to His saying {إله وَاحِدٌ}" is that it conjoined a clause to a single word, so it must be interpreted as a single word, because it conjoined to the khabar and so it is a khabar. On its being a conjunction, it may also conjoin to the whole clause, namely His saying {إِنَّمَا هُوَ إله وَاحِدٌ}; and it is as though Ibn ʿAṭiyya meant this by "wāw of beginning", for it is resumptive.

semin-durr:114-114.t: The words of the Exalted: {واشكروا نِعْمَةَ الله}: He explicitly mentioned the blessing here because it was mentioned before together with those who were ungrateful for it; that did not come in al-Baqara, rather He said: {واشكروا للَّهِ} [al-Baqara: 172], since that had not preceded there; and parallels of it have preceded here.

semin-durr:116-116.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَلاَ تَقُولُواْ لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الكذب}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the kāf, kasra on the dhāl and the accusative on the bāʾ (الكَذِبَ). There are four views on it. The most apparent: it is in the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by «تَصِفُ», with «ما» maṣdariyya (infinitival); the object of the saying is then the clause in His words {هذا حَلاَلٌ وهذا حَرَامٌ}, and {لِمَا تَصِفُ} is the reason for the prohibition of saying that, i.e. do not say "this is lawful and this is forbidden" because of your tongues' describing the lie. Al-Zajjāj and al-Kisāʾī inclined to this. The meaning is: do not declare lawful or forbidden on account of a saying your tongues utter without proof.
The second: it is in the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the saying, and His words {هذا حَلاَلٌ} are a badal (substitute) of «الكذب», because it is the same thing; or it is the object of an implied verb, i.e. "so that they say: this is lawful and this is forbidden"; and {لِمَا تَصِفُ} is also a reason, the implied form being: "and do not say the lie because of your tongues' describing". Is it possible for the matter to be one of tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one word) on this view — that is, the saying requires «الكذب» and «تَصِفُ» also requires it, i.e. "and do not say the lie for what your tongues describe it"? This is open to question.
The third: it is in the accusative as a badal of the omitted pronoun returning to «ما», if we say that it is in the sense of "that which", the implied form being: لِما تصفُه (for what [your tongues] describe it); al-Ḥūfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned that. The fourth: it is in the accusative by an implied "I mean" (أعني); Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and there is no need for it, nor any meaning on it.
Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Yaʿmar and Ṭalḥa read «الكذبِ» in the genitive, and there are two views on it. The first: it is a badal of the relative, i.e. "and do not say, because of your tongues' describing — the lie", or "because of that which your tongues describe — the lie"; He made it the lie itself, because it is that. The second, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī: it is a naʿt (adjective) of the maṣdariyya «ما». The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this on the grounds that the grammarians have stipulated that the maṣdar formed from أنْ and the verb is not qualified by an adjective — one does not say «يعجبني أن تخرجَ السريعُ» (your swift going out pleases me) — and there is no difference between this and the other maṣdariyya particles.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Muʿādh ibn Jabal read it with ḍamma on the kāf and the dhāl and the nominative on the bāʾ (الكُذُبُ), as an adjective of the tongues, like صَبُور and صُبُر; or as the plural of كاذِب, like شارِف and شُرُف; or as the plural of «كِذاب», like كِتاب and كُتُب.
Maslama ibn Muḥārib read it likewise, according to what Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmitted, except that he put the bāʾ in the accusative (الكُذُبَ), and there are three views on it, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī. The first: it is in the accusative by way of reviling (al-shatm), meaning that it is originally an adjective of the tongues, as in the preceding reading. The second: it is in the sense of "the lying words", meaning that it is a mafʿūl bihi, governed either by «تَصِفُ» or by the saying, as has passed, i.e. "do not say the lying words", or "because of your tongues' describing the lying words". The third: it is the plural of الكِذاب from your saying «كَذِب كِذاباً», meaning that it is in the accusative as a maṣdar, because it is of the meaning of the tongues' describing; so it is like كُتُب as the plural of كِتاب. Al-Kisāʾī read {وَلاَ كِذَاباً} without doubling, as will come in al-Nabaʾ.
His words: «لِتَفْتَرُوا»: there are three views on the lām. The first: al-Wāḥidī said: "It is a badal of {لِمَا تَصِفُ}, because their describing the lie is a fabrication against Allah." The Shaykh said: "This is on the assumption of making «ما» maṣdariyya. But if it is in the sense of 'that which', the lām in it is not for causation, such that something that conveys causation could be substituted for it; rather the lām in «لِما» is attached to «لا تقولوا» in the same way as it is attached in your saying: لا تقولوا لِما أَحَلَّ اللهُ: هذا حرامٌ (do not say of what Allah has made lawful: this is forbidden), i.e. do not call the lawful forbidden; and as you say: لا تقلْ لزيدٍ عمراً (do not call Zayd ʿAmr), i.e. do not apply this name to him." I say: although this is apparent, it does not prevent causation being intended, even if it is in the sense of "that which".
The second: it is the lām of outcome (al-ṣayrūra), since they did not do it for that purpose.
The third: it is for explicit causation, and it is not far-fetched that the like of that should proceed [from them].

semin-durr:117-117.t: The words of the Exalted: {مَتَاعٌ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «قليل» is its khabar (predicate). This is open to question because of beginning with an indefinite noun without a justification. If it is claimed that it is annexed, like "their enjoyment is little", that is very far-fetched. The second: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. their remaining, or their living, or their benefit in what they are upon [is a brief enjoyment].

semin-durr:118-118.t: The words of the Exalted: {مِن قَبْلُ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «حَرَّمْنَا» or to «قَصَصْنَا». The muḍāf ilayhi of «قبلُ» is implied as: "and before Our forbidding to the people of your religion".

semin-durr:119-119.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مِن بَعْدِهَا}: i.e. after the doing of evil, the repentance and the reform. It is said: [it refers] to the ignorance. And it is said: to the evil, because it is in the sense of المعصية (disobedience, feminine).
And «بجهالة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «عَمِلوا».

semin-durr:120-120.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أُمَّةً}: الأُمَّة is applied to a man who combines praiseworthy traits. It is also said: [it is on the pattern] fuʿla, indicating intensity. Ibn Hāniʾ [Translator's note: i.e. Abū Nuwās, al-Ḥasan ibn Hāniʾ] looked to the first meaning in his words:
302 - 4- وليس الله بمُسْتَنْكَرٍ ... أن يَجْمَعَ العالمَ في واحِدِ
(It is not deemed strange of Allah that He should gather the world in a single man.) [Translator's note: the verse is commonly cited as «وليس على الله بمستنكر»; translated as printed.]

semin-durr:121-121.t:
The words of the Exalted: {شَاكِراً}: it may be a third khabar (predicate), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of one of the two pronouns in «قانِتاً» or «حنيفاً».
His words: «لأَنْعُمِهِ» may be attached to «شاكراً» or to «اجتباه». And «اجتباه» is either a ḥāl or another khabar of kāna. And {إلى صِرَاطٍ} may be attached to «اجتباه» and to «هداه», according to the rule of tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one word).

semin-durr:123-123.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ثُمَّ أَوْحَيْنَآ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "In this «ثم» there is what there is of magnifying his rank and exalting his station, and of making known that the most honourable of the marks of esteem granted to the Friend of the All-Merciful, and the most exalted of the blessings bestowed on him, is the following of him by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; because it indicates the remoteness of this attribute in rank above all the other attributes with which Allah praised him."
His words: {أَنِ اتبع}: it may be the explicative (mufassira) أن, or the maṣdariyya (infinitival), in which case it together with the verb it governs is the object of the revealing.
His words: «حنيفاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its verification has preceded in al-Baqara. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Makkī said: it — meaning حنيفاً — cannot be a ḥāl of «إبراهيم», because it is a muḍāf ilayhi. It is not as he said, because prepositions may govern the ḥāl when they govern the one to whom the ḥāl belongs, as in your saying «مررتُ بزيدٍ قائماً» (I passed by Zayd standing)." I say: what Makkī mentioned about the impossibility of a ḥāl of the muḍāf ilayhi is not unrestricted, because of what has preceded in detail in al-Baqara. As for Ibn ʿAṭiyya's saying that the governor is the genitive-governing particle, it is not so; the governor is only what the genitive-governing particle is attached to; that is why, when the particle is dropped, its genitive noun is put in the accusative.

semin-durr:124-124.t: The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ}: the majority read it in the passive, and Abū Ḥaywa in the active, with «السَّبْتَ» as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

semin-durr:125-125.t: The words of the Exalted: {ادع}: its object may be intended, i.e. "call the people", or not, i.e. "perform the calling". And «بالحكمة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. accompanied by it.

semin-durr:126-126.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ}: the majority read it on the pattern mufāʿala (fāʿala), which is in the sense of faʿala, like سافَر. Ibn Sīrīn read «عَقَّبْتم» with doubling, meaning: "if you follow up, then follow up with the like of what was done to you". It is also said: "if you pursue". The bāʾ is for transitivity, and in the reading of Ibn Sīrīn it is either causal or redundant (zāʾida).
His words: {لِّلصَّابِرينَ}: it may be general, i.e. patience is better for the genus of the patient; or it may be a case of the overt noun standing in place of the pronoun, i.e. your patience is better for you.

semin-durr:127-127.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِلاَّ بالله}: i.e. with His help; so it [the bāʾ] is for seeking help (al-istiʿāna).
His words: {فِي ضَيْقٍ}: Ibn Kathīr [read it] here and in al-Naml with kasra on the ṣād [Translator's note: so in the source; the letter is the ḍād], and the rest with fatḥa. It is said: they are two dialectal forms with one meaning in this maṣdar, like القَوْل and القِيْل. It is also said: the form with fatḥa is a lightened form of «ضَيِّق», like مَيْت from «مَيِّت», i.e. in a narrow matter. Al-Fārisī rejected this on the grounds that the adjective is not specific to the noun it describes, so the omission [of the noun described] cannot be claimed; that is why «مررت بكاتبٍ» (I passed by a writer) is permitted and «بآكلٍ» (by an eater) is not.
His words: {مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «ضَيْق». And «ما» is maṣdariyya or in the sense of "that which", the returning pronoun being omitted.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا بِكُم}: two views are possible for «ما». One: it is a relative noun, the prepositional phrase being its ṣila (relative clause), and it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being His saying {فَمِنَ الله}, with the fāʾ redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar because the relative noun carries the sense of a condition; its implied form is: "and that which is established with you". {مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ} is an explanation of the relative noun. Some estimated what «بكم» is attached to as a specific [verb], saying: "and whatever has befallen you or come down upon you"; this is not good, since only a general being (kawn muṭlaq) is estimated.
The second: it is conditional, and the verb of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) after it is omitted; al-Farrāʾ inclined to this, and al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The implied form is: and whatever is with you." This was rejected on the ground that a verb is omitted only after «إنْ» specifically, in two places. One: in the construction of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), as in {وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ المشركين استجارك} [al-Tawba: 6], because the omitted is as though mentioned. The second: when «إنْ» is followed by the negative «لا», and what precedes it in the speech indicates the protasis, as in his saying:
298 - 2- فطلِّقْها فَلَسْتَ لها بكُفْءٍ ... وإلاَّ يَعْلُ مَفْرِقَك الحُسامُ
(So divorce her, for you are no match for her; and if not, the sword will come down on the parting of your hair.)
i.e. "and if you do not divorce her"; it was omitted because his saying «فَطَلِّقْها» indicates it. If the negative «لا» is not present, or the particle is other than «إنْ», it is not omitted except by poetic licence. An example of the first:
298 - 3- قالَتْ بناتُ العمِّ يا سَلْمَى وإنْ ... كان غنياً مُعْدِماً قالت: وإنْ
(The cousins said: "O Salmā, even if he is poor and destitute?" She said: "Even if.")
i.e. "and even if he were rich, I would be content with him". [Translator's note: the explanation as printed ("rich") does not match the verse's «فقيراً/غنياً» wording; translated as written.] An example of the second:
298 - 4- صَعْدَة نابتةٌ في حائرٍ ... اَيْنَما الريحُ تُمَيِّلْها تَمِلْ
(A straight shoot growing in a hollow: wherever the wind bends it, it bends.)
And another's saying:
298 - 5- فمتى واغِلٌ يَنُبْهُمْ يُحَيُّو ... هـ وتُعْطَفْ عليه كأسُ الساقي
(Whenever an uninvited guest comes upon them, they greet him, and the cupbearer's cup is turned towards him.)
His saying: {فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْأَرُونَ}: the fāʾ is [in] the answer of «إذا». Al-juʾār is raising the voice; Ruʾba said, describing a monk: /
298 - 6- يُراوِحُ مِنْ صلواتِ المَلِي ... كِ طَوْراً سُجوداً وطَوْراً جُؤاراً
(He alternates in the prayers to the King — now prostrating, now crying aloud (juʾār).)
Some restricted it to crying for help, and al-Zamakhsharī recited:
298 - 7- جَآَّرُ ساعاتِ النيامِ لربِّه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Crying aloud to his Lord in the hours when others sleep …)
It was said: al-juʾār is like al-khuwār; jaʾara al-thawru and khāra are one [i.e. the bull lowed], except that this one has hamza as its middle radical and that one a weak letter. Al-Rāghib said: "Jaʾara: when one goes to excess in supplication and humble entreaty, by likening to the lowing of wild animals."
Al-Zuhrī read «تَجَرون», dropping the hamza and casting its vowel onto the quiescent letter before it, just as Nāfiʿ read «رِدَّاً» for «رِدْءاً». [Translator's note: the attested reading of Nāfiʿ is «رِدًا»; printed here with a shadda.]

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذَا كَشَفَ}: the first «إذا» is conditional and the second is of surprise (fujāʾiyya), its answer. The verse contains evidence that the conditional «إذا» is not governed by its answer, because what follows the «إذا» of surprise does not govern what precedes it.
Qatāda read «كاشَفَ» on the pattern fāʿala. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense of faʿala, and it is stronger than «كَشَفَ», because the form of contest (mughālaba) indicates intensiveness."
His saying: «منكم»: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «فريق», with «مِنْ» partitive, and it may be for explanation. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "As though He said: then a disbelieving party — and they are you."

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَكْفُرُواْ}: there are three views on this lām. The first: it is the lām of kay (purpose), attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يُشْركون», i.e. the cause of their associating [partners] is their disbelief in Him. The second: it is the lām of becoming (lām al-ṣayrūra), i.e. their affair came to that. The third: it is the lām of command, and al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this.
Abū al-ʿĀliya read — and Makḥūl narrated it from Abū Rāfiʿ, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from him ﷺ — «فَيُمْتَعُوا» with ḍamma on the yāʾ (dots beneath), sukūn on the mīm and fatḥa on the tāʾ, the imperfect of mutiʿa in the passive; and {فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ} also with the yāʾ (dots beneath). In this reading, the dropping of the nūn in this imperfect may be either for the accusative (subjunctive), conjoined to «ليكفروا», if it is the lām of kay or of becoming; or also for the accusative, but as the answer to a command, if the lām is for command. And its dropping may be for the jussive, conjoined to «لِيَكْفُروا», also if it is for command.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِمَا لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ}: the pronoun in «يَعْلمون» may be for the disbelievers, i.e. "for what the disbelievers do not know"; and the meaning of their not knowing them is that they call them gods and believe that they harm, benefit and hear, while the matter is not so. And it may be for the gods, namely the idols, i.e. "for things not characterised by knowledge".
«نصيباً» is the first object and the prepositional phrase before it is the second, i.e. "and they assign to the idols a share". {مِّمّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ} may be a naʿt (adjective) of «نصيباً», or attached to (mutaʿalliq) the [verb of] assigning; so «مِنْ» on the first view is partitive, and on the second for the beginning [of the extent].

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَهُمْ مَّا يَشْتَهُونَ}: two views are possible on it. One: this is a clause made up of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. they assign daughters to Allah; then He informed that they have what they desire. Al-Farrāʾ, al-Ḥawfī, al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «ما» to be in the position of an accusative, conjoined to «البناتِ», and «لهم» conjoined to «الله», i.e. "and they assign to themselves what they desire".
The Shaykh said: "They overlooked a grammatical rule, namely that the verb of an attached pronoun does not pass over to its own attached pronoun except in the category of ẓanna and in ʿadima and faqada; and there is no difference whether the verb passes over by itself or by a preposition. So 'Zaydun ḍarabahu', i.e. he struck himself, is not permissible, nor 'Zaydun marra bihi', i.e. he passed by himself; but 'Zaydun ẓannahu qāʾiman' and 'Zaydun faqadahu' and 'ʿadimahu' are permissible, i.e. he thought himself standing, and he lost himself and lacked himself. Since this is established, making «ما» accusative, conjoined to «البنات», leads to the verb of an attached pronoun — namely the wāw of / «يَجْعَلون» — passing over to its own attached pronoun, namely «هم» in «لهم»." End of quotation, in summary.
What he mentioned needs more clarification than this, so I say about it briefly: know that the verb of an attached pronoun, and the verb of an overt noun, may not pass over to their own attached pronoun except in the category of ẓanna and its sisters among the verbs of the heart, and in faqada and ʿadima. So "Zaydun ḍarabahu" and "ḍarabahu Zaydun", meaning he struck himself, are not permissible; while "Zaydun ẓannahu qāʾiman" and "ẓannahu Zaydun qāʾiman", "Zaydun faqadahu wa-ʿadimahu" and "faqadahu wa-ʿadimahu Zaydun" are permissible. And the verb of an attached pronoun may not pass over to its overt [antecedent] in any category: "Zaydan ḍaraba", i.e. he struck himself, is not permissible.
In my saying "to their own attached pronoun" there are two restrictions. One: its being a pronoun; if it were an overt noun such as al-nafs (self), it would not be barred, as in "Zaydun ḍaraba nafsahu" and "ḍaraba nafsahu Zaydun". The second: its being attached; if it were detached it would be permissible, as in "Zaydun mā ḍaraba illā iyyāhu" and "mā ḍaraba Zaydun illā iyyāhu". The reasons and proofs of this question belong to a place other than this one, and I have set them out thoroughly in Sharḥ al-Tashīl.
Makkī said: "This is not permissible according to the Basrans, just as 'jaʿaltu lī ṭaʿāman' (I made food for me) is not permissible [Translator's note: printed «يحوز», evidently for «يجوز»]; only 'jaʿaltu li-nafsī ṭaʿāman' (I made food for myself) is permissible. Had the wording of the Qurʾān been «ولأنفسِهم ما يَشْتَهون», what al-Farrāʾ said would be permissible according to the Basrans. This is a principle that needs much explanation and expansion."
I say: what he alluded to of the prohibition you already know — praise be to Allah — from what I have set before you.
The Shaykh, after reporting from al-Farrāʾ and those who followed him that «ما» is in the position of an accusative, said: "Abū al-Baqāʾ said — having reported it —: 'and there is reservation (naẓar) about it'." I say: Abū al-Baqāʾ did not place the reservation on this view; he placed it only on the weakening of it on the ground that it leads to the verb of an attached pronoun passing over to its own attached pronoun outside what is excepted. For he said: "Some people declared this view weak and said: had it been so, He would have said «ولأنفسهم»; and there is reservation about that." So he placed the reservation on the weakening of it, not on it.
It may be said: the ground of the reservation is that what is barred is that verb's passing over, i.e. its falling upon what is made genitive by the preposition, as in "Zaydun marra bihi", for the passing falls on Zayd; but in what we are dealing with, the assigning does not fall on those who assign, but on what they desire. The Shaykh used constantly to object to the rule given above with His saying, the Exalted: {وهزى إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النخلة} [Maryam: 25] and {واضمم إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 32]; and the answer to both is what has already been given, namely that the shaking and the drawing-in do not fall on the kāf. This has already been given by us in another place; I have repeated it only because of its difficulty, and because this [place] is distinguished by an additional benefit.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ}: it [«ظلّ»] may keep its proper sense of denoting remaining through the daytime in the state attributed to its subject (ism), or it may be in the sense of «صار» (became); on both estimations it is incomplete (nāqiṣa), and «مُسْوَدّاً» is its khabar (predicate). As for «وجهُه», there are two views on it. The well-known one — which is what first comes to mind — is that it is its ism. The second: it is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in «ظل», a substitute of part for whole, i.e. "one of them remained — his face", i.e. the face of one of them remained.
His saying: «كَظِيم»: it may be in the sense of fāʿil (active participle), or in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), as in His saying {وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ} [al-Qalam: 48]. The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «ظَلَّ», or from «وجهه», or from the pronoun in «ظَلَّ». [Translator's note: "or from the pronoun in «ظَلَّ»" is repeated in the source.] Abū al-Baqāʾ said here: "Had it been read «مُسْوَدٌّ»" — meaning in the nominative — "it would be sound, on the basis that you make the ism of «ظَلَّ» implied, and the clause its khabar." And he said in Sūrat al-Zukhruf: "Both are read in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the khabar of «ظلَّ»."

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يتوارى}: it may be resumptive, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from whatever the first [clause] was a ḥāl from — except [from] «وجهُه», for that does not suit it; and it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «كظيم».
His saying: {مِنَ القوم مِن سواء}: two prepositional phrases with the same wording are attached here because their meanings differ: the first is for the beginning [of the extent] and the second is causal, i.e. "because of the evil of what he was given tidings of". [Translator's note: the Quranic text reads «مِن سُوءِ»; printed in the source as «مِن سواء».]
His saying: {أَيُمْسِكُهُ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "In the position of a ḥāl, its implied form being: he hides, hesitating whether to keep it or not." This is a mistake according to the grammarians, because they have stated that a ḥāl cannot be a request (ṭalabī) clause. What appears [correct] is that this interrogative clause is governed by something omitted, which is a ḥāl from the agent of «يتوارى» completing the sentence, i.e. "he hides, considering or thinking: shall he keep it in humiliation".
The majority read the pronouns as masculine, in regard to the wording of «ما»; and / al-Jaḥdarī read {أَيُمْسِكُها}, {أَمْ يَدُسُّها}, in regard to the female or the meaning of «ما». It was also read {أَيُمْسِكُهُ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ}.
Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā read «على هَوان», on the pattern of «قَذَال», and a group «على هَوْنٍ» with fatḥa on the hāʾ, which is awkward here, because «الهَوْن» with fatḥa is gentleness and softness, and its meaning does not suit here; as for «الهَوان», it has the meaning of «هُوْن» with ḍamma.
His saying: {على هُونٍ}: there are two views on it. One: it is a ḥāl from the agent; this is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: he keeps her while accepting humiliation and against his will.
The second: it is a ḥāl from the object, i.e. he keeps her abased and humiliated.
Al-dass: concealing a thing; here it is an expression for burying alive (al-waʾd).

semin-durr:62-62.t:
