His saying, the Exalted: {أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ الكذب}: the majority [read it] with «الكذبَ» as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and {أَنَّ لَهُمُ الحسنى} is a badal (substitute) from it, a substitute of the whole for the whole, or [accusative] by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "that theirs is the best".
Al-Ḥasan read «أَلْسِنَتْهُمْ» with sukūn on the tāʾ for lightening; it resembles the sukūn on the lām in {بلى وَرُسُلُنَا لَدَيْهِمْ يَكْتُبُونَ} [al-Zukhruf: 80], and on the hamza of «بارِئْكم», and the like.
Al-alsina is the plural of «لِسان» when it is treated as masculine, so it is pluralised as masculine fiʿāl is pluralised, as in ḥimār / aḥmira; and when it is treated as feminine it is pluralised on afʿul, like dhirāʿ / adhruʿ.
Muʿādh ibn Jabal read «الكُذُبُ» with ḍamma on the kāf and the dhāl and the bāʾ in the nominative, as the plural of kadhūb, like ṣabūr / ṣubur, which follows the rule; it was said: the plural of kādhib, like shārif / shuruf, as in her saying:
398 - 8- ألا يا حَمْزُ للشُّرُفِ النَّواءِ ... ………. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O Ḥamza, [up] for the fat old she-camels …) [Translator's note: the verse number is printed «398 - 8» in the source, evidently for 298 - 8.]
but this does not follow the rule. In that case it is a naʿt (adjective) of «ألسنتهم», and then {أَنَّ لَهُمُ الحسنى} is a mafʿūl bihi. The discussion of «لا جَرَمَ» has already been given in full in Hūd.
His saying: {وَأَنَّهُمْ مُّفْرَطُونَ}: Nāfiʿ read it with kasra on the rāʾ, an active participle from afraṭa, when one exceeds [the bounds]; the meaning is that they exceed the limit in disobeying Allah the Exalted; so afʿala here is intransitive. The rest read it with fatḥa, a passive participle from afraṭtuhu, and it has two meanings. One: it is from "afraṭtuhu behind me", i.e. I left him and forgot him; al-Farrāʾ reported that the Arabs say "afraṭtu minhum nāsan", i.e. I left some people behind; and the meaning is that they are forgotten and left in the Fire. The second: it is from afraṭtuhu, i.e. I sent him ahead to such-and-such, transferred by the hamza from faraṭa ilā kadhā, i.e. he went ahead to it; so the Shaykh said, and he recited from al-Quṭāmī:
298 - 9- واسْتَعْجَلُونْا وكانوا مِنْ صحابَتِنا ... كما تَعَجَّلَ فُرَّاطٌ لِوُرَّادِ
(They hurried ahead of us, though they were of our company, as forerunners (furrāṭ) hurry ahead for those coming to water.)
So he made faraṭa intransitive and afraṭa transferred [to transitivity]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense that they are sent ahead to the Fire and hasten to it, from afraṭtu fulānan and faraṭtuhu when I sent him ahead to the water"; so he made faʿala and afʿala the same in meaning, not afʿala transferred from faʿala. Both views are possible. From it is al-faraṭ, i.e. the one who goes ahead. He said, upon him be peace: "I am your forerunner (faraṭ) at the Pool", i.e. the one who precedes you. And from it: "and make him a forerunner (faraṭ) and a treasure", i.e. going ahead with intercession and the weighting of the scales.
Abū Jaʿfar read — in one transmission — «مُفَرِّطون» with doubled rāʾ with kasra, from farraṭa fī kadhā, i.e. he fell short; and in another transmission with fatḥa, from farraṭtuhu, made transitive by doubling from faraṭa without doubling, i.e. he went ahead and preceded.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Ḥasan read «لا جَرَمَ إنَّ لهم النارَ وإنهم» with kasra on «إنَّ» in both, on the basis that it is the answer to an oath for which «لا جَرَمَ» suffices.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمُ اليوم}: this clause may be a narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl māḍiya), i.e. "so he is their helper", or of a future one, with «اليوم» meaning the Day of Resurrection; this is when the pronoun refers back to «أُمَم», which is the apparent view.
Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to refer back to Quraysh, so that it would be a description of a present state, neither past nor future. He also allowed it to refer back to «أمم», but with the omission of a muḍāf, its implied form being: "so he is the patron of the likes of them today". The Shaykh considered that far-fetched. It is as though what led him [al-Zamakhsharī] to that was His saying «اليومَ», for it is an adverb of the present; but it has already been said that it is by way of narrating a past or future state.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً}: there are two views on it. One: both are accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose), governed by «أَنْزَلْنَا». Since the agent of the cause and of what is caused is the same, the verb reached them by itself; and since it is not the same in His saying «وما أنْزَلْنا إلاَّ لِتُبَيِّن» — because the agent of the sending down is Allah and the agent of the making clear is the Messenger / — the verb reached the cause by means of the particle, so it was said {إِلاَّ لِتُبَيِّنَ}, i.e. "in order that you make clear"; though this lām is not required from another respect, namely that its genitive is «أن», and there is disagreement on the particulars of this question.
This is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's words, for he said: "They are conjoined to the position of «لِتُبَيِّنَ», except that they are accusative as objects of purpose, because they are the act of the one who sent down the Book; and the lām entered on «لتبيِّنَ» because it is the act of the one addressed, not the act of the one who sends down; and only what is the act of the agent of the verb explained by the cause is made accusative as an object of purpose." The Shaykh said: "His saying 'conjoined to the position of «لتبيِّنَ»' is not correct, because its position is not accusative so that an accusative could be conjoined [to it]. Do you not see that, had he made it accusative, it would not be permissible, because the agent differs?"
I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not make the accusative result from conjunction to the position; he made it result only from the verb's reaching them directly because the agent is the same, as he stated explicitly in what I have just reported from him. He made the conjunction only for the sake of association in being causes, nothing else, meaning that they are two causes, just as «لتبيِّنَ» is a cause. And even if we grant that it was made accusative by conjunction to the position, that does no harm. His saying "because its position is not accusative" is not granted; it is something on which there is no disagreement, that the position of a prepositional phrase is accusative, because it is an extra element (faḍla), unless it stands in place of a nominative. Do you not see their explanation of His saying {وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ} [al-Māʾida: 6], in the reading with the accusative, as conjoined to the position of «برؤوسكم»? And they allow "marartu bi-Zaydin wa-ʿAmran" (I passed by Zayd and ʿAmr [acc.]) — with a disagreement over whether that is regular by analogy or not, not over the basic question. This is a good point of inquiry which the one being refuted left aside.

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {نُّسْقِيكُمْ}: this clause may be an explanation of the lesson (al-ʿibra), as though it were said: "What is the lesson?" and it was said: "We give you to drink, from between digested matter and blood, pure milk." It may be the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being the answer to that question, i.e. "it — i.e. the lesson — is: We give you to drink"; and it would then be like their saying: "That you hear of the Muʿaydī is better than that you see him."
Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read «نَسْقيكم» with fatḥa on the nūn, here and in al-Muʾminūn, and the rest with ḍamma in both. People disagreed: are saqā and asqā two dialectal forms with one meaning, or is there a difference between them? It is a well-known disagreement. It was said: they are of one meaning, and [the following] was recited combining the two forms:
229 - 0- سَقَى قومي بني مَجْدٍ وأسْقَى ... نُمَيْراً والقبائلَ من هلالِ
(May He give drink (saqā) to my people, Banū Majd, and give drink (asqā) to Numayr and the tribes of Hilāl.) [Translator's note: the verse number is printed «229 - 0» in the source, evidently for 299 - 0.]
He prayed for rain and fertility for all of them. «نُمَيْراً» is the second object, i.e. "sweet (numayr) water". [Translator's note: translated as written; the gloss treats «نميراً» as "sweet water" although in the verse it reads as the tribe Numayr.] Abū ʿUbayd said: "For one who gives drink to the lips: saqā only; for one who waters trees and land: asqā; and for one who prays for rain and the like: asqā only." Al-Azharī said: "The Arabs say, of what is from the bellies of livestock, from the sky, or a flowing river: asqaytu, i.e. I made it a drink for him and made for him a supply of drink from it; and when it is for the lips they say saqā, and do not say asqā."
Al-Fārisī said: "Saqaytuhu until he was quenched [Translator's note: printed «ختى», evidently for «حتى»], and asqaytuhu a river, i.e. I made it a drink for him." It was said: saqāhu when he hands him the vessel to drink from, and of this one does not say asqāhu.
Abū Rajāʾ read «يُسْقِيْكم» with ḍamma on the yāʾ (dots beneath), and there are two views on its agent. One: it is Allah the Exalted. The second: it is the pronoun of al-naʿam (cattle), indicated by «الأنعام», i.e. cattle that are made a supply of drink for you. It was also read «تَسْقيكم» with fatḥa on the tāʾ (dots above). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is weak." The Shaykh said: "Its weakness in his view — and Allah knows best — is that it is feminine in «تَسْقِيْكم» and masculine in His saying {مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ}; but there is no weakness in that respect, because the masculine and the feminine are by two different considerations." I say: its weakness in his view is from the side of meaning, namely that the aim is to remind creation of the favour, so ascribing the giving of drink to Allah the Exalted is what is fitting, not ascribing it to the livestock.
His saying: {مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ}: «مِنْ» may be partitive, or for the beginning of the extent. The pronoun here refers back to «الأنعام» as singular masculine. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Sībawayh mentioned al-anʿām in the chapter on 'what is diptote' among the singular nouns that come on the pattern afʿāl, as in their saying 'thawbun akyāsh' (a garment of [twisted] yarn), and for that reason the pronoun refers back to it in the singular. As for «في بطونها» in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn, it is because its meaning is plural. It may be said that there are two views on «الأنعام». One: it is the broken plural of «نَعَم», like ajbāl from jabal. And [the other:] it is a singular noun entailing the meaning of a plural [like naʿam]. When it is treated as masculine, it is as «نَعَم» is treated as masculine in his saying:
299 - 1- في كل عام نَعَمٌ تَحْوُوْنَهُ ... يَلْقِحُه قومٌ وتَنْتِجُونَهْ
(Every year there are cattle (naʿam) that you seize; a people impregnate it, and you deliver its young.)
And when it is treated as feminine, there are two views on it: that it is the broken plural of «نَعَم», and that it has the meaning of a plural."
The Shaykh said: "As for what he mentioned from Sībawayh, in his book, in 'This is the chapter on what is on the pattern mafāʿil and mafāʿīl', this is his text: 'As for ajmāl and fulūs, they are triptote, and what resembles them, because they resemble the singular. / Do you not see that you say aqwāl / aqāwīl, aʿrāb / aʿārīb, and aydin / ayādin? So these words go over to the pattern mafāʿil and mafāʿīl, just as the singular goes over to it when it is given a broken plural. As for mafāʿil and mafāʿīl, they are not given a broken plural, so the plural does not go over to any pattern other than this, because this pattern is the limit; so since they [ajmāl and fulūs] resembled the singular, they were made triptote.' Then he said: 'Likewise fuʿūl: if you gave a broken plural to the like of fulūs, in order to pluralise them all, you would take it over to faʿāʾil, as you say jadūd / jadāʾid and rakūb / rakāʾib; whereas if you did that with mafāʿil and mafāʿīl, you would not go beyond this pattern. What strengthens that is that some of the Arabs say ʾutiyy, with ḍamma on the alif. As for afʿāl, it sometimes occurs for the singular; among the Arabs are some who say: huwa al-anʿām. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {نُّسْقِيكُمْ مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ}. And Abū al-Khaṭṭāb said: I heard some Arabs say: this is a garment akyāsh.'"
He [the Shaykh] said: "What Sībawayh mentioned is the difference between mafāʿil and mafāʿīl on the one hand and afʿāl and fuʿūl on the other — even though all of them are plural patterns — in that mafāʿil and mafāʿīl cannot be pluralised, while afʿāl and fuʿūl can go over to a pattern resembling mafāʿil or mafāʿīl. So since these two can go over to that, they are triptote, while mafāʿil and mafāʿīl are diptote, because those two resemble the singular in that they can be pluralised, and these two cannot be pluralised. Then their resemblance to the singular was strengthened by the fact that some Arabs say for ʾatiyy: ʾutiyy, with ḍamma on the hamza — meaning that fuʿūl has rarely come, not as a maṣdar, for the singular — and by the fact that some Arabs may apply afʿāl to the singular, in that they make the pronoun singular and say: 'huwa al-anʿām'. He only means that this is figurative, because al-anʿām has the meaning of al-naʿam, and al-naʿam is singular, as he said:
299 - 2- تَرَكْنا الخيلَ والنَّعَمَ المُفَدَّى ... وقلنا للنساءِ بها أَقيمي
(We left the horses and the cherished cattle (al-naʿam), and said to the women there: stay.)
For that reason Sībawayh said: 'As for afʿāl, it sometimes occurs for the singular'; his saying 'it sometimes occurs for the singular' is evidence that this is not by original coinage. So al-Zamakhsharī's saying 'he mentioned it among the singular nouns on the pattern afʿāl' is a distortion of the wording, and he understood from Sībawayh what he did not intend. What indicates what we have said is that Sībawayh, where he mentioned the patterns of singular nouns, stated explicitly that afʿāl is not one of their patterns. Sībawayh said in the chapter on triliterals that have received an augment: 'There is not in the language ufʿīl, nor afʿawl, nor ufʿāl, nor afʿīl, nor afʿāl, unless a noun is given it as a broken plural.'" He said: "This is an explicit statement by him that afʿāl does not occur among singular nouns."
I say: what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is the apparent sense of Sībawayh's expression, and it is sufficient to justify the pronoun referring back in the singular; and if afʿāl may occur in place of the singular figuratively, that does not harm what we are concerned with. He did not distort his wording, nor did he understand from him something other than what he intended, given what I have mentioned of the meaning he intended.
It was said: the pronoun was made masculine only because it refers back to a part, namely the females, because the males have no milk; so it is as though the lesson lies in some of the livestock. Al-Kisāʾī said: "I.e. in the bellies of what He mentioned." Al-Mubarrad said: "This is common in the Qurʾān. The Exalted said: {كَلاَّ إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُ} [ʿAbasa: 11–12], i.e. remembered this thing. And the Exalted said: {فَلَماَّ رَأَى الشمس بَازِغَةً قَالَ هذا رَبِّي} [al-Anʿām: 78], i.e. this rising thing. This happens only with figurative feminine; 'your slave-girl went (masc.)' is not permissible." I say: on that basis his saying was explained:
299 - 3- فيها خطوطٌ مِنْ سوادٍ وبَلَقْ ... كأنه في الجِلدِ تَوْليْعُ البَهَقْ
(In it are streaks of black and piebald white, as though it (masc.) were, on the skin, the patches of vitiligo.)
i.e. as though what was mentioned. It was said: a broken plural of non-rational things is treated as a collective (jamāʿa) and as a plural; in this sūra the meaning of plural was considered, and in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn the meaning of collective was considered. Of the first is the poet's saying: /
299 - 4- مثل الفراخِ نُتِفَتْ حواصِلُهْ ...
(Like the fledglings whose (masc. sing.) crops were plucked.)
It was said: [it is because] a singular that conveys plurality can take its place, for «نَعَم» can take its place, and «نَعَم» conveys plurality. Like it is his saying:
299 - 5- وطابَ أَلْبانُ الِّلقاحِ وبَرَدْ ...
(And the milks of the milch-camels were good and cool (masc. sing.).)
because «لَبَن» (milk) can take its place. And like it is their saying "huwa aḥsanu al-fityāni wa-ajmaluhu" (he is the finest of the young men and the most handsome of it), i.e. the finest young man; except that this is not regular by analogy according to Sībawayh [Translator's note: printed «سييويه»] and his followers.
Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned six views, five of which have already come in the course of what I have mentioned. The sixth: it refers back to the stallion, because milk comes from the stallion's covering the she-camel, so the origin of the milk is the stallion's [water]. He said: "This is weak, because although the milk is attributed to the stallion, He made 'bellies' plural, and the stallion of the livestock is not one, nor does one have bellies. If it is said: He meant the genus — it has already been mentioned." He means that it has already been said that the masculine is by consideration of the genus of livestock, so there is no need to estimate its referring back to «فَحْل» meaning the genus. I say: this view was reported by Makkī from Ismāʿīl al-Qāḍī, and he did not follow it with any objection.
His saying: {مِن بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ}: several views are possible on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the giving of drink, on the basis that it is for the beginning of the extent; if we make what precedes it the same, then its genitive must be a badal (substitute) from the genitive of the first «مِنْ», lest two [particles] identical in wording and meaning be attached to one governor, which is impossible. It is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because a place includes what is in it. If you make it [the first] partitive, the matter is easy.
The second: it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «لَبَناً», since had it come after it, it would, with its genitive, be a naʿt (adjective) of it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was placed first only because it is the locus of the lesson, so it is worthy of being placed first."
The third: it, with its genitive, is a ḥāl from the relative noun before it.
Al-farth: the residue of fodder remaining in the rumen, and the dense residue of food remaining in the intestine. One says: faratha kabidahu, i.e. he crumbled it; and afratha fulānun fulānan: he plunged him into a calamity that is like farth.
His saying: «لَبَنا»: it is the second object of «نُسْقي». It was also read «سَيِّغاً» with a doubled yāʾ, on the pattern of «سَيِّد», and its morphology is like its morphology. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar lightened it, as in mayt and hayn. It may not be of the pattern faʿl, since then it would have to be «سَوْغاً», like qawl.

semin-durr:67-67.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِن ثَمَرَاتِ النخيل}: there are four views on it. The first: it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [verb]; al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as: "And We give you to drink from the fruits of the date-palms and the grapevines, i.e. from their juice; it was omitted because «نُسْقيكم» before it indicates it." He said: "And «تَتَّخذون» is an explanation and disclosure of the manner of giving drink." Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated it as: "He created for you and made for you."
What al-Zamakhsharī estimated is more fitting. It should not be said: "There is no need to estimate «نُسْقيكم»; rather His saying {وَمِن ثَمَرَاتِ} is conjoined to His saying {مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ}, so it conjoins some of the dependents of the first verb to others, as you say 'I gave Zayd to drink of milk and of honey', with no need to estimate a verb before your saying 'of honey'." That should not be said, because the «نُسْقيكم» that is actually uttered came as an explanation of the lesson of the livestock, so it is not fitting for this to be attached to it, since it is not part of the lesson connected with the livestock. The Shaykh said: "It was said: it is attached to «نُسْقيكم», so it is conjoined to {مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ}; or to an omitted «نُسقيكم» indicated by «نُسْقِيكم»." End of quotation. He did not follow it with any objection, and it is open to what I have just set out.
The second: it is attached to «تَتَّخذون», and «منه» is a repetition of the adverbial phrase for emphasis, as in "Zayd is in the house, in it"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. On this view there are six views on the hāʾ in «منه». One: it refers back to the omitted muḍāf, namely the juice, just as [the pronoun] in His saying {أَوْ هُمْ قَآئِلُونَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 4] referred back to the omitted "people". The second: it refers back to the meaning of «الثمرات», because it has the meaning of al-thamar (fruit). The third: it refers back to «النخيل». The fourth: it refers back to the genus. The fifth: it refers back to the part. The sixth: it refers back to what was mentioned.
The third of the first [four] views: it is conjoined to His saying {فِي الأنعام}, so in meaning it is the khabar (predicate) of the ism of «إنَّ» in His saying {وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الأنعام لَعِبْرَةً}, the implied form being: "and indeed for you in the livestock and in the fruits of the date-palms there is a lesson"; and His saying «تتخذون» is an explanation and exposition of the lesson, just as «نُسْقِيكم» also came as an explanation of it.
The fourth: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); al-Ṭabarī estimated it as: "And of the fruits of the date-palms is what you take [Translator's note: printed «تتَّحذون», evidently for «تتَّخذون»]." / The Shaykh said: "That is not permissible on the school of the Basrans." I say: there is reservation about that, because he could say: this «ما» is not a relative noun but an indefinite noun qualified by a description, and the omission of the qualified noun is permissible while the description is a clause, because «مِنْ» is in the sentence; and whenever «مِنْ» is in the sentence, the omission is regular, as in "of us [some] departed and of us [some] stayed". For this reason Makkī compared it to His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 164], i.e. "except one who has a station".
He said: "So «مَنْ» was omitted because «مِنْ» in His saying «وما مِنَّا» indicates it." When al-Zamakhsharī estimated the qualified noun, he estimated it as "fruit that you take", and compared it to the poet's saying:
299 - 6- يَرْمي بكفِّيْ كان مِنْ أَرْمى البشر ...
(He shoots with the two hands of [one who] was among the best of men at shooting.)
its implied form being "with the two hands of a man", except that the omission in the verse is anomalous because «مِنْ» is absent. When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned this view, he said: "It was said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted [noun], its implied form being 'something (shayʾan) that you take from it', in the accusative, i.e. 'and indeed of the fruits of the date-palms …'. Or if you wish, «شيء» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with {مِن ثَمَرَاتِ} as its khabar."
Al-sakar — with two fatḥas — there are several views on it. The first: it is one of the names of wine, as in the poet's saying:
299 - 7- بئس الصُّحاةُ وبئس الشَّرْبُ شَرْبُهُمُ ... إذا جَرَى فيهم المُزَّاءُ والسَّكَرُ
(Wretched are they when sober, and wretched is their drinking company, when al-muzzāʾ and al-sakar [kinds of wine] flow among them.)
The second: it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), then wine was named by it. One says: sakira, yaskaru, sukran and sakaran, like rashida, yarshadu, rushdan and rashadan. The poet said:
299 - 8- وجاؤُوْنا بهم سَكَرٌ علينا ... فَاَجْلَى اليومُ والسَّكْران صاحي
(They came at us with an intoxication (sakar) of rage against us; then the day cleared, and the drunk one was sober.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The third: it is a name for vinegar in the language of Abyssinia; Ibn ʿAbbās said this. The fourth: it is a name for juice as long as it is sweet, as though it were so named because of what it would become if left. The fifth: it is a name for food (al-ṭuʿm); Abū ʿUbayda said this, and recited:
299 - 9- جَعَلْتَ أعراضَ الكرامِ سَكَراً ...
(You have made the honour of noble men your sakar [food / a thing to relish].)
i.e. you feed on their honour. It was said about the verse that it is from wine, and that when he violated people's honour it was as though he became intoxicated with it.
His saying: {وَرِزْقاً حَسَناً}: it may be a conjunction of different things, which is the apparent view — in the exegesis: it is like raisins, vinegar and the like — or a conjunction of descriptions one upon another, i.e. "you take from it what combines intoxicant and good provision", as in his saying:
300 - 0- إلى المَلِكِ القَرْمِ وابن الهُمامِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(To the king, the chief, and the son of the noble lord …)
— the verse.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أتى أَمْرُ الله}: regarding «أتى» there are two aspects. One, which is the well-known one: that it is past in wording but future in meaning, since what is meant by it is the Day of Resurrection; it is brought out in the form of what has occurred and passed only to confirm it and for the truthfulness of the One who reports it. The second: that it is in its usual sense, and what is meant by it is its preliminaries and beginnings, which is the support of His Messenger ﷺ.
His saying: {فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ}: regarding the accusative pronoun there are two aspects. The more apparent: that it refers to the matter (al-amr), for it is what is being spoken of. The second: that it refers to Allah, that is: "do not seek to hasten His punishment."
His saying: {عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ}: «ما» may be maṣdar-forming, in which case there is no returning pronoun according to the majority, that is: "above their associating others with Him"; or it may be a relative noun.
The majority read {فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ} with tāʾ, as address to the believers or to the disbelievers. Ibn Jubayr [read it] with yāʾ, referring to the disbelievers or the believers.
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «تُشْرِكُون» with the tāʾ of address, following the address in «تَسْتَعْجِلُوه», and the rest with yāʾ, referring to the disbelievers. Al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa, al-Jaḥdarī and a great multitude read with tāʾ in both verbs.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يُنَزِّلُ الملائكة}: the disagreement over «يُنَزِّل», regarding doubling and lightening, has been mentioned in al-Baqara. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Aʿmash and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «تَنَزَّلُ» doubled, as a passive, with a tāʾ, and «الملائكةُ» nominative because it stands in the place of the agent. Al-Jaḥdarī read likewise, except that he lightened the zāy. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Abū l-ʿĀliya and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim read «تَنَزَّلُ» with a single tāʾ and doubled zāy, as an active; the original is «تَتَنَزَّل» with two tāʾs. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «نُنَزِّلُ» with two nūns and doubled zāy, «الملائكةَ» accusative, and Qatāda likewise except that he lightened. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "There is an irregularity in both," without explaining its reason; its reason is that what precedes it and follows it is a latent third person, and its analysis is by a shift of person (iltifāt).
His saying «بالرُّوْحِ»: it may be attached to the sending down itself, or to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الملائكة», that is: "and with them the Spirit."
His saying: {مِنْ أَمْرِهِ}: a ḥāl from «الرُّوحِ». And «مِنْ» is either for explaining the genus or for partition.
His saying: {أَنْ أنذروا}: regarding «أَنْ» there are three aspects. The first: that it is the explicative (mufassira), because revelation contains a kind of saying, and sending down with the Spirit is an expression for revelation. The second: that it is the lightened form of the heavy, and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), its implied form being: «أنَّ الشأنَ أقولُ لكم: إنه لا إله إلا أنا»; al-Zamakhsharī said it. The third: that it is the maṣdar-forming one, which by nature puts the imperfect in the accusative, and is connected with the imperative, as in their saying «كتبت إليه بأنْ قُمْ» ("I wrote to him: Stand!"); and we have had a discussion of this earlier.
If we say that it is the explicative, it has no position; and if we say that it is the lightened or the subjunctive one, then regarding its position there are three aspects. The first: that it is genitive in position as a badal (substitute) of «الرُّوح», because affirmation of divine oneness is a spirit by which souls live. The second: that it is in the position of genitive by omission of the governing preposition, as is the position of al-Khalīl. The third: that it is in the position of accusative by its omission, which is the position of Sībawayh, the original being «بأَنْ أَنْذِروا»; when the preposition was omitted, the well-known disagreement applied.
His saying: {أَنَّهُ لاَ إله إِلاَّ أَنَاْ}: it is the object of the warning, and the warning may be in the sense of informing. It is said «نَذَرْتُه» and «أَنْذَرته بكذا», that is: "inform them of the oneness [of Allah]." And His saying «فاتَّقونِ» is a shift (iltifāt) to the first person after the third.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن نُّطْفَةٍْْ}: attached to «خَلَق», and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent. Al-nuṭfa: a drop of water; «نَطَفَ رأسُه ماءً», that is, it dripped. It was also said: it is clear water, and it is used to express the water of the man, and is a euphemism for the pearl; from it comes «صبيٌّ مُنَطَّف» when there is a pearl in his ear, and one says «ليلة نَطُوف» when rain comes in it. Al-nāṭif: what flows of liquids, «نَطَفَ يَنْطِفُ», that is, it flowed, so it is nāṭif. And «فرنٌ يَنْطِفُ بسوءٍ» [as written in the source].
His saying: {فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ}: He conjoined this clause to what precedes it. If it is said: the fāʾ indicates immediate succession, especially as «idhā», which requires suddenness, has been found with it, whereas his being a manifest disputant did not follow immediately upon his creation from a drop; many intermediate stages came between them. The answer has two aspects. One: that it belongs to expressing the state of a thing by what it comes to, like His saying, the Exalted: {أَعْصِرُ خَمْراً} [Yūsuf: 36]. The second: that He thereby alluded to the speed with which they forget the beginning of their creation. It was also said: there are omitted intermediate stages. What appears is that His saying «خَلَقَ» is an expression for bringing him into existence and rearing him until he reaches the stage of these two attributes.
And «خصيم» is faʿīl, a form of intensity, from «خَصَم» in the sense of «اختصم»; it may also be in the sense of «مُخاصِم», like «al-khalīṭ» and «al-jalīs».
[Translator's note: the phrase «وفرنٌ يَنْطِفُ بسوءٍ» in the first paragraph appears as written in the source; its wording looks corrupt (perhaps «وقَرْنٌ» or similar), and I have not emended it.]

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والأنعام خَلَقَهَا}: the majority read with accusative, and there are two aspects in it. One: accusative by preoccupation (ishtighāl), which is preferable to nominative because a verbal clause precedes. The second: that it is accusative as a conjunction to «الإنسان»; al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it, so «خَلَقَها» on this is an emphasis, while on the first it is an explicator. «والأنعامُ» was read nominative in an irregular reading, and it is the less preferred.
His saying: {لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ}: «لكم» may be attached to «خَلَقَها», that is, for your sake and your benefits, with «فيها» a fronted khabar (predicate) and «دِفْءٌ» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). It may be that «لكم» is the khabar, with «فيها» attached to what the khabar is attached to; or «فيها» a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «دِفْء», because were it to come after it, it would be an adjective of it; or «فيها» is the khabar, with «لكم» attached to what it is attached to, or a ḥāl from «دِفْء»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected it, saying that when the governing element of the ḥāl is abstract, it does not precede the whole clause: «قائماً في الدار زيدٌ» is not permissible; if it comes after, as in «زيدٌ في الدار قائماً», it is permissible without disagreement; and if it comes in the middle, there is disagreement — al-Akhfash allowed it and others forbade it.
I say: someone could say that since the governing element precedes it and it is with it, it is permissible to put it before it as it stands; unless he says that putting it before it when it is postponed does not entail putting it before it when it is advanced, due to the increase in ugliness.
Abū l-Baqāʾ also said: "«دِفْء» may be nominative by «لكم» or by «فيها», and the whole clause is a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun." The Shaykh said: "It is not called a clause; for the implied form is: «خلقها كائناً لكم فيها دفءٌ» or «خَلَقها لكم كائناً فيها دِفْءٌ»." I say: the disagreement has been mentioned earlier about the implied element to which the preposition phrase is attached when it falls as a ḥāl, adjective or predicate: is it implied as a verb or a noun? Perhaps Abū l-Baqāʾ inclined to the first, so his calling it a clause is correct on this view.
Al-dif': a noun for that with which one is warmed, that is, heated; its plural is adfāʾ; «دَفِئَ يومُنا فهو دَفِىءٌ» (our day grew warm), «دَفِئَ الرجلُ يَدْفَأُ دَفاءَةً ودَفَاءً فهو دَفْآنُ» (the man grew warm), and the feminine is «دَفْأَى», like «sakrān» and «sakrā». Al-mudfaʾa, lightened or doubled: camels with abundant fur and fat. It was said: al-dif' is the offspring of camels, their milk and what is of benefit from them.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «دِفٌ» by transferring the vowel of the hamza to the fāʾ, and al-Zuhrī likewise, except that he doubled the fāʾ, as though he treated connected reading like pausing, as in their saying «هذا فَرُخّْ» with doubling in pause. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "Some of them compensate for this hamza by doubling the fāʾ, and it is one of the two ways of Ḥamza ibn Ḥabīb in pause." I say: doubling in pause is an independent dialect, even if nothing is omitted from the word on which one pauses.
His saying: {وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ}: «مِنْ» here is for the beginning of the extent, and partition here is weak. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: putting the adverbial first announces specificity, and one may eat from other than them. I say: eating from them is the principle on which people rely; as for others, such as ducks, chickens and the like of game, they are as though not counted."
